bf.caregiver-mental-illness-or-substance.cw: Growing up with a parent who struggled with their mental health, drinking, or drugs.
bf.caregiver-mental-illness-or-substance.ex: A father who drank heavily every evening.

bf.invalidating-environment.def: Caregivers often dismissed, punished or trivialized the child's emotional experiences, teaching that feelings are wrong or must be hidden.
bf.invalidating-environment.cw: Growing up being told your feelings were wrong, silly, or not allowed.
bf.invalidating-environment.ex: "Stop crying or I'll give you something to cry about."

bf.learned-fear.def: Fear acquired by watching others react fearfully, or through repeated warnings and threat information, rather than through direct harm.
bf.learned-fear.cw: Learning to fear something by seeing others afraid of it, or being warned about it often.
bf.learned-fear.ex: A mother who screamed and left the room at every spider.

bf.early-illness-experience.def: Serious illness, hospital stays or medical crises in childhood, or witnessing a family member's serious illness or death from illness.
bf.early-illness-experience.cw: Being seriously ill as a child, or seeing someone close become very ill.
bf.early-illness-experience.ex: A grandparent's sudden heart attack at a family dinner.

bf.prior-trauma-exposure.def: Earlier exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence, not captured by the childhood abuse categories.
bf.prior-trauma-exposure.cw: Something terrifying that happened to you, or that you saw, earlier in your life.
bf.prior-trauma-exposure.ex: Survived a house fire at age 20.

bf.discrimination-and-minority-stress.def: Ongoing stress from stigma, prejudice and discrimination tied to a minority identity, including expected rejection and concealment.
bf.discrimination-and-minority-stress.cw: Stress from being treated unfairly or judged because of who you are.
bf.discrimination-and-minority-stress.ex: Years of racist comments at school and at work.

bf.socioeconomic-disadvantage.def: Growing up or living with poverty, food or housing insecurity, limited education, or chronic financial strain.
bf.socioeconomic-disadvantage.cw: Not having enough money, food, safe housing, or chances in life, growing up or now.
bf.socioeconomic-disadvantage.ex: Family relied on food banks throughout childhood.

bf.behavioral-inhibition.def: A lasting tendency since early childhood toward reticence, fearfulness and withdrawal in new situations or with unfamiliar people.
bf.behavioral-inhibition.cw: Being naturally shy or cautious since you were little, especially with new people or places.
bf.behavioral-inhibition.ex: Clung to a parent and would not speak at preschool for months.

bf.high-negative-emotionality.def: A temperament of strong, frequent negative emotion and stress reactivity, with a sense that threats are hard to manage.
bf.high-negative-emotionality.cw: Having always felt emotions strongly and gotten stressed or upset easily.
bf.high-negative-emotionality.ex: Described since childhood as a worrier who was easily upset.

bf.impulsive-temperament.def: A lasting tendency to act quickly without planning and to seek novelty or excitement despite possible risks.
bf.impulsive-temperament.cw: Tending to act on the spur of the moment or chase excitement, even when it is risky.
bf.impulsive-temperament.ex: Started drinking heavily and driving fast in early adolescence.

bf.family-history-of-mental-illness.def: Biological relatives with depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, psychosis, substance use or other mental disorders, indicating inherited vulnerability.
bf.family-history-of-mental-illness.cw: Blood relatives who have had mental health or addiction problems.
bf.family-history-of-mental-illness.ex: Mother and maternal aunt both treated for recurrent depression.

bf.adhd.def: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), or lifelong attention, impulse and organization difficulties that shape learning, self-esteem and coping.
bf.adhd.cw: Lifelong trouble with focus, restlessness, or organization, with or without an ADHD diagnosis.
bf.adhd.ex: Repeatedly told at school to try harder and stop daydreaming.

bf.autism.def: Autism or autistic traits: differences in social communication, sensory processing and need for sameness that shape experience and stress.
bf.autism.cw: Being autistic, or having autistic traits, like finding social rules confusing or senses overwhelming.
bf.autism.ex: Diagnosed autistic at 30 after years of feeling different.

bf.learning-or-intellectual-disability.def: Intellectual disability or a specific learning disorder, such as dyslexia, affecting learning, school experience and self-image.
bf.learning-or-intellectual-disability.cw: Having a learning difficulty like dyslexia, or finding learning much harder than others did.
bf.learning-or-intellectual-disability.ex: Dyslexia not recognized until college, after years of failing tests.

bf.brain-injury-or-birth-complications.def: Early neurological insult, such as birth complications or head injury, or later acquired brain injury, that increases vulnerability.
bf.brain-injury-or-birth-complications.cw: A head injury, or problems around your birth, that may have affected how your brain works.
bf.brain-injury-or-birth-complications.ex: Concussion with loss of consciousness at age 15.

bf.chronic-physical-condition.def: An ongoing medical condition, chronic pain or physical disability that adds stress, limits activity, or affects brain and body functioning.
bf.chronic-physical-condition.cw: A long-term health problem, ongoing pain, or disability that affects your daily life.

bf.previous-episodes.def: Earlier episodes of the same or a related mental health problem, which raise the risk of further episodes.
bf.previous-episodes.cw: Having had this problem, or something like it, before.
bf.previous-episodes.ex: Third episode of depression since age 18.

bf.social-isolation.def: Few close relationships, or no confiding relationship, leaving the person without someone to turn to under stress.
bf.social-isolation.cw: Not having people close to you, or anyone you can really talk to.
bf.social-isolation.ex: Moved for work and has no friends in the new city.

bf.bereavement.def: The death of a family member, partner, friend or other important person.
bf.bereavement.cw: Someone important to you has died.
bf.bereavement.ex: Husband died suddenly six months ago.

bf.relationship-breakup.def: The end of a romantic relationship or marriage, whether the person or the partner ended it.
bf.relationship-breakup.ex: Partner of eight years left for someone else.

bf.job-loss.def: Losing a job through dismissal, layoff or business failure, or prolonged unemployment, with loss of income, role and structure.
bf.job-loss.cw: Losing your job, or being out of work for a while.
bf.job-loss.ex: Laid off after 15 years when the factory closed.

bf.work-or-study-stress.def: Sustained pressure, conflict or change at work or in education, such as overload, a difficult manager, a new role or exams.
bf.work-or-study-stress.cw: Ongoing pressure or problems at work or school, like too much work or a difficult boss.
bf.work-or-study-stress.ex: A new manager doubled targets and criticized the team publicly.

bf.financial-crisis.def: A sudden or worsening money problem, such as major debt, eviction threat, bankruptcy or loss of benefits.
bf.financial-crisis.cw: Serious money trouble, like big debts, possible eviction, or losing your income.
bf.financial-crisis.ex: Received a final eviction notice after falling behind on rent.

bf.new-illness-or-injury.def: Onset or diagnosis of a significant physical illness, injury or surgery, or a sudden worsening of an existing condition.
bf.new-illness-or-injury.cw: Getting a serious illness, injury, or diagnosis, or an existing one getting worse.
bf.new-illness-or-injury.ex: Diagnosed with breast cancer in the spring.

bf.perinatal-period.def: Pregnancy, childbirth and the months after birth, including difficult or traumatic births and pregnancy loss.
bf.perinatal-period.cw: Pregnancy, having a baby, a difficult birth, or losing a pregnancy.
bf.perinatal-period.ex: Emergency cesarean followed by weeks of broken sleep.

bf.relocation-or-migration.def: Moving home, city or country, including migration and forced displacement, with loss of familiar networks, roles and routines.
bf.relocation-or-migration.cw: Moving to a new home, city, or country, especially leaving people and routines behind.
bf.relocation-or-migration.ex: Arrived as a refugee two years ago, separated from extended family.

bf.recent-traumatic-event.def: A recent event involving actual or threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence, experienced, witnessed, or happening to someone close.
bf.recent-traumatic-event.cw: Something frightening happened recently where you, or someone close, could have died or been badly hurt.
bf.recent-traumatic-event.ex: Held at knifepoint during a robbery last month.

bf.relationship-difficulties.def: Persistent conflict, distance or dissatisfaction in a key relationship with a partner, family member or close friend.
bf.relationship-difficulties.cw: Ongoing trouble, arguments, or distance in an important relationship.
bf.relationship-difficulties.ex: Months of daily arguments with a teenage son.

bf.caregiving-burden.def: Providing substantial ongoing care for an ill, disabled or older family member, straining time, sleep, finances and well-being.
bf.caregiving-burden.cw: Looking after a family member who is ill, disabled, or elderly, and the strain it brings.
bf.caregiving-burden.ex: Caring full time for a parent with dementia.

bf.role-transition.def: A major change in social role, such as leaving home, starting college, marriage, children leaving home, or retirement.
bf.role-transition.cw: A big change in your role in life, like leaving home, marrying, or retiring.
bf.role-transition.ex: Retired after 40 years and lost daily structure.

bf.legal-problems.def: Involvement in legal proceedings, such as arrest, criminal charges, lawsuits, custody disputes or immigration hearings.
bf.legal-problems.cw: Trouble with the law or court cases, like an arrest, custody fight, or immigration case.
bf.legal-problems.ex: Facing a custody hearing next month.

bf.medication-change.def: Starting, stopping or changing the dose of a psychiatric or other medication, including stopping without medical advice.
bf.medication-change.cw: Starting, stopping, or changing a medicine, especially stopping without your prescriber's advice.
bf.medication-change.ex: Stopped an antidepressant abruptly when planning a pregnancy.

bf.substance-use-change.def: Starting or increasing alcohol, cannabis, stimulant or other drug use, which can precipitate or worsen mental health problems.
bf.substance-use-change.cw: Starting to use, or using more, alcohol or drugs.
bf.substance-use-change.ex: Daily high-potency cannabis use in the months before first psychotic symptoms.

bf.goal-attainment-event.def: Achieving a significant goal or a major positive life change, which can precipitate manic symptoms in bipolar disorder.
bf.goal-attainment-event.cw: A big success or exciting positive change in your life.
bf.goal-attainment-event.ex: Promotion to partner, followed by weeks of little sleep.

bf.sleep-schedule-disruption.def: A life change that disrupts sleep timing or daily rhythms, such as shift work, long-haul travel, newborn care or lost routine.
bf.sleep-schedule-disruption.cw: Changes that throw off your sleep or daily rhythm, like night shifts, travel, or a new baby.
bf.sleep-schedule-disruption.ex: Moved to rotating night shifts in March.

bf.humiliating-event.def: An event in which the person was publicly embarrassed, shamed, or devalued in a core role, such as being exposed or demoted.
bf.humiliating-event.cw: Something happened where you felt deeply embarrassed, shamed, or put down in front of others.
bf.humiliating-event.ex: Froze during a presentation while colleagues laughed.

bf.social-support.def: Relationships that give emotional, practical or informational support, including at least one person the client can confide in.
bf.social-support.cw: People you can turn to for comfort, help, or advice, including someone you can really talk to.
bf.social-support.ex: A sister the client calls most evenings.

bf.secure-early-relationship.def: At least one warm, reliable caregiver or other adult in childhood who offered safety, comfort and encouragement.
bf.secure-early-relationship.cw: Having had at least one adult growing up who made you feel safe and cared for.
bf.secure-early-relationship.ex: A grandmother who always made time to listen.

bf.coping-skills.def: Existing abilities to solve problems, regulate emotions, plan and seek help that the person already uses in some areas of life.
bf.coping-skills.cw: Ways of coping you already use well, like solving problems, calming down, or asking for help.
bf.coping-skills.ex: Manages emergencies calmly at work as a nurse.

bf.personal-strengths.def: Enduring positive qualities, such as persistence, kindness, humor, curiosity or courage, that can be harnessed in therapy.
bf.personal-strengths.cw: Good qualities you have, like being determined, kind, funny, or brave.
bf.personal-strengths.ex: Kept a household running through years of a partner's illness.

bf.values-and-purpose.def: Clear personal values, goals or commitments that give life meaning and motivate change.
bf.values-and-purpose.cw: Things that matter deeply to you and give your life meaning or direction.
bf.values-and-purpose.ex: Wants to be a patient, present father to two young children.

bf.faith-or-spiritual-community.def: Religious or spiritual beliefs, practices or community that provide comfort, meaning, belonging or support.
bf.faith-or-spiritual-community.cw: Faith, spiritual practice, or a religious community that gives you comfort, meaning, or support.
bf.faith-or-spiritual-community.ex: Attends weekly services and is supported by the congregation.

bf.community-belonging.def: A sense of belonging to a cultural, identity-based or local community that provides pride, support and shared coping.
bf.community-belonging.cw: Feeling part of a community, culture, or group where you belong and feel supported.
bf.community-belonging.ex: Active member of a local LGBTQ+ sports club.

bf.meaningful-occupation.def: Paid work, study, volunteering or another valued role that provides structure, income or social contact, and self-worth.
bf.meaningful-occupation.cw: Work, study, volunteering, or another role that gives your days structure and purpose.
bf.meaningful-occupation.ex: Volunteers at an animal shelter three mornings a week.

bf.material-stability.def: Secure income, stable housing and access to basic resources, reducing daily stress and making engagement in care easier.
bf.material-stability.cw: Having enough money and a safe, stable place to live.
bf.material-stability.ex: Has a steady income and a long-term lease.

bf.interests-and-hobbies.def: Hobbies, interests and activities the person enjoys or used to enjoy, which can be rebuilt as sources of pleasure and mastery.
bf.interests-and-hobbies.cw: Hobbies and activities you enjoy, or used to enjoy.
bf.interests-and-hobbies.ex: Used to play guitar in a band in college.

bf.past-successful-coping.def: Times the person managed difficulty, recovered from an earlier episode or overcame adversity, showing strategies and resilience to draw on.
bf.past-successful-coping.cw: Times you got through something hard, or recovered before.
bf.past-successful-coping.ex: Recovered from a depressive episode at 25 with exercise and support.

bh.overt-avoidance.def: Not entering, or arranging life to stay away from, feared or unpleasant situations, places, people, activities or tasks.
bh.overt-avoidance.cw: Staying away from places, people or tasks that make you anxious or upset.
bh.overt-avoidance.ex: Turning down a work presentation because of fear of blushing.

bh.subtle-avoidance.def: Entering a feared situation but limiting contact with it, such as avoiding eye contact, staying at the edges or engaging only partly.
bh.subtle-avoidance.cw: Going along but holding back, so you never fully face what scares you.
bh.subtle-avoidance.ex: Attending a party but staying in the kitchen and avoiding conversation.

bh.escape.def: Leaving a situation once anxiety or distress rises, which ends exposure before the feared outcome can be disconfirmed.
bh.escape.cw: Getting out of a situation as soon as the feelings get too strong.
bh.escape.ex: Leaving the supermarket line when the heart starts racing.

bh.interoceptive-avoidance.def: Avoiding activities, foods or drinks that produce feared bodily sensations, such as exercise, caffeine, heat, sex or excitement.
bh.interoceptive-avoidance.cw: Steering clear of anything that makes your heart race or your body feel strange.
bh.interoceptive-avoidance.ex: Stopping exercise because a fast heartbeat feels like the start of a heart attack.

bh.trauma-reminder-avoidance.def: Avoiding people, places, conversations, objects or activities that bring back memories of a traumatic event.
bh.trauma-reminder-avoidance.cw: Keeping away from anything that reminds you of what happened.
bh.trauma-reminder-avoidance.ex: Taking a long detour to avoid driving past the site of the crash.

bh.distraction-to-avoid.def: Habitually busying the mind or hands to keep feared thoughts, images, memories or feelings out of awareness.
bh.distraction-to-avoid.cw: Keeping yourself busy or distracted so you never have to think about it or feel it.
bh.distraction-to-avoid.ex: Keeping music on constantly so memories of the assault cannot surface.

bh.procrastination.def: Voluntarily delaying an intended task despite expecting to be worse off, often to avoid discomfort, boredom or fear of failure.
bh.procrastination.cw: Putting things off even though you know waiting will make things harder.
bh.procrastination.ex: Leaving the tax forms untouched until the night before the deadline.

bh.numbing-activities.def: Low-effort activities such as scrolling, gaming or television, used for long periods to escape low mood or problems.
bh.numbing-activities.cw: Losing hours to your phone, games or TV to escape how you feel.
bh.numbing-activities.ex: Scrolling social media in bed for three hours instead of replying to emails.

bh.in-situation-safety-behavior.def: An action taken within a feared situation to prevent a feared catastrophe, which stops the person learning it would not have happened.
bh.in-situation-safety-behavior.cw: Something you do to feel safe that stops you finding out you would be okay anyway.
bh.in-situation-safety-behavior.ex: Gripping a shopping cart tightly to avoid fainting.

bh.safety-objects.def: Keeping items believed to prevent or rescue from catastrophe, such as medication, water, a phone or a particular bag.
bh.safety-objects.cw: Always needing certain things with you, just in case something bad happens.
bh.safety-objects.ex: Never leaving home without anxiety medication, even though it is rarely taken.

bh.relying-on-safe-person.def: Entering feared situations only with a trusted companion, or keeping them reachable, to feel protected from catastrophe.
bh.relying-on-safe-person.cw: Only going places if someone you trust is with you or a phone call away.
bh.relying-on-safe-person.ex: Shopping only when a partner comes along.

bh.concealing-anxiety-signs.def: Efforts to hide visible anxiety, such as covering blushing, gripping objects to stop shaking or wearing dark clothes to hide sweat.
bh.concealing-anxiety-signs.cw: Trying hard to hide that you are nervous so others will not notice.
bh.concealing-anxiety-signs.ex: Wearing a scarf to hide neck blushing during meetings.

bh.mental-rehearsal.def: Mentally preparing and checking sentences before and while speaking, to avoid saying something wrong or appearing foolish.
bh.mental-rehearsal.cw: Practicing what to say in your head and checking every word as you talk.
bh.mental-rehearsal.ex: Silently rehearsing an introduction while others are speaking.

bh.reassurance-seeking.def: Repeatedly asking others, or oneself, for confirmation that a feared outcome will not happen or that one has done nothing wrong.
bh.reassurance-seeking.cw: Asking again and again if things are okay, even after you have been told.
bh.reassurance-seeking.ex: Asking a partner five times a day whether the door was definitely locked.

bh.checking.def: Repeatedly verifying that something is safe, correct or done, beyond what is needed, to prevent harm or reduce doubt.
bh.checking.cw: Going back to check things over and over to make sure nothing bad happens.
bh.checking.ex: Returning home three times to make sure the stove is off.

bh.washing-cleaning.def: Excessive or ritualized washing, showering or cleaning, performed to remove feared contamination or to feel clean enough.
bh.washing-cleaning.cw: Washing or cleaning far more than needed until it finally feels clean enough.
bh.washing-cleaning.ex: Washing hands for ten minutes after touching a door handle.

bh.ordering-arranging.def: Arranging objects or doing actions until they feel exactly right, symmetrical or complete, to relieve discomfort or prevent harm.
bh.ordering-arranging.cw: Needing things lined up or done just right, and feeling awful until they are.
bh.ordering-arranging.ex: Straightening books on a shelf until they feel exactly even.

bh.repeating-counting.def: Repeating actions, words or counts a set number of times, or until it feels right, to prevent harm or discomfort.
bh.repeating-counting.cw: Doing something again and again, or counting, until it feels safe or right.
bh.repeating-counting.ex: Switching the light on and off six times before leaving a room.

bh.mental-ritual.def: Covert compulsions such as praying, counting, repeating phrases or mentally reviewing events, done to prevent harm or reduce doubt.
bh.mental-ritual.cw: Things you do in your head over and over to feel safe or sure.
bh.mental-ritual.ex: Mentally replaying a conversation to check nothing offensive was said.

bh.neutralizing.def: Voluntary attempts to cancel, undo or put right an intrusive thought or its feared consequences, overtly or in the mind.
bh.neutralizing.cw: Trying to cancel out or undo an upsetting thought so it cannot cause harm.
bh.neutralizing.ex: Thinking a "safe" word after an unwanted image of harming someone.

bh.excessive-acquiring.def: Repeated buying, collecting or taking free items beyond need or space, with distress at passing them up.
bh.excessive-acquiring.cw: Bringing home more things than you need or have room for, and finding it hard to stop.
bh.excessive-acquiring.ex: Buying extra kitchen tools on every shopping trip despite full cupboards.

bh.saving-items.def: Keeping possessions regardless of value and avoiding discarding them, leading to clutter that limits use of living spaces.
bh.saving-items.cw: Keeping things because getting rid of them feels too hard or wrong.
bh.saving-items.ex: Keeping stacks of old newspapers that block a hallway.

bh.body-focused-repetitive-behavior.def: Repetitive hair pulling, skin picking, nail biting or similar acts causing damage, often triggered by tension, boredom or perceived imperfections.
bh.body-focused-repetitive-behavior.cw: Pulling, picking or biting at your hair, skin or nails, often without meaning to.
bh.body-focused-repetitive-behavior.ex: Picking at facial skin for an hour while studying.

bh.social-withdrawal.def: Reducing contact with others, declining invitations or isolating, which removes social reward and support.
bh.social-withdrawal.cw: Pulling away from friends and family and spending more time alone.
bh.social-withdrawal.ex: Ignoring friends' messages and missing a weekly game night.

bh.inactivity.def: Marked reduction in routine, pleasurable or goal-directed activity, often spending long periods in bed or on the couch.
bh.inactivity.cw: Doing much less than before, and spending long stretches resting or lying down.
bh.inactivity.ex: Staying on the couch most of the day instead of going for usual walks.

bh.neglecting-self-care.def: Letting basic routines lapse, such as hygiene, meals, chores, bills or medical care, which adds problems and lowers mood.
bh.neglecting-self-care.cw: Letting everyday things like washing, eating well or chores slide.
bh.neglecting-self-care.ex: Not showering for several days and leaving dishes and mail piling up.

bh.binge-eating.def: Eating an objectively large amount of food in a discrete period, with a sense of loss of control over eating.
bh.binge-eating.cw: Eating a very large amount at once and feeling unable to stop.
bh.binge-eating.ex: Eating several packs of cookies in half an hour after a stressful call.

bh.dietary-restriction.def: Deliberately limiting how much, when or what is eaten, guided by strict dietary rules, to control shape or weight.
bh.dietary-restriction.cw: Strictly limiting food because of rules about what, when or how much you can eat.
bh.dietary-restriction.ex: Eating nothing before 6 p.m. and avoiding all bread.

bh.compensatory-behaviors.def: Acts used to undo the feared effects of eating, such as self-induced vomiting or misuse of laxatives or diuretics.
bh.compensatory-behaviors.cw: Trying to get rid of food or calories after eating.
bh.compensatory-behaviors.ex: Purging after a binge to feel less "full of food".

bh.driven-exercise.def: Exercise that feels compelled, rigid or excessive, done to control shape or weight or to compensate for eating.
bh.driven-exercise.cw: Feeling you must exercise, even when ill or tired, to make up for eating.
bh.driven-exercise.ex: Running every day despite an injury after eating dinner.

bh.emotional-eating.def: Eating, not necessarily a binge, in response to moods or events rather than hunger, to soothe or numb feelings.
bh.emotional-eating.cw: Eating to feel better when upset, bored or stressed, not because you are hungry.
bh.emotional-eating.ex: Reaching for chocolate after every argument.

bh.body-checking.def: Repeatedly scrutinizing, measuring, weighing or pinching the body to assess shape, weight or appearance.
bh.body-checking.cw: Checking your body over and over, in mirrors, by pinching or by weighing.
bh.body-checking.ex: Pinching stomach fat and checking thigh size many times a day.

bh.body-avoidance.def: Avoiding seeing, being seen or knowing about the body, such as avoiding mirrors, scales, tight clothes or photographs.
bh.body-avoidance.cw: Avoiding mirrors, scales, photos or clothes that show your body shape.
bh.body-avoidance.ex: Refusing to be weighed and wearing only baggy clothes.

bh.camouflaging.def: Hiding or disguising a perceived appearance flaw with makeup, clothing, posture or hairstyle, or by excessive grooming.
bh.camouflaging.cw: Covering up or fixing a part of your looks you believe is flawed.
bh.camouflaging.ex: Wearing a cap indoors to hide perceived thinning hair.

bh.symptom-checking.def: Repeatedly examining the body or monitoring functions, such as pulse or lumps, for signs of serious illness.
bh.symptom-checking.cw: Checking your body again and again for signs that something is seriously wrong.
bh.symptom-checking.ex: Pressing on a lymph node several times a day to see if it has grown.

bh.seeking-medical-tests.def: Repeatedly consulting doctors or requesting tests and scans to rule out illness, gaining only brief relief.
bh.seeking-medical-tests.cw: Going to doctors or asking for tests over and over to be sure you are not ill.
bh.seeking-medical-tests.ex: Booking a third scan after two normal results.

bh.symptom-searching.def: Repeated online or other searching about symptoms and illnesses, which often raises anxiety rather than settling it.
bh.symptom-searching.cw: Looking up symptoms online again and again, then feeling more worried.
bh.symptom-searching.ex: Spending the evening reading forums about a headache.

bh.avoiding-medical-care.def: Avoiding doctors, tests, health information or illness reminders out of fear of bad news.
bh.avoiding-medical-care.cw: Staying away from doctors or anything about illness because you fear what you might hear.
bh.avoiding-medical-care.ex: Ignoring a cancer screening invitation for two years.

bh.substance-use-to-cope.def: Using alcohol, drugs or medication beyond prescription to reduce distress, face situations or get to sleep.
bh.substance-use-to-cope.cw: Drinking, using drugs or taking extra medication to feel calmer or forget.
bh.substance-use-to-cope.ex: Drinking two glasses of wine before a party to calm nerves.

bh.self-harm.def: Intentional self-poisoning or self-injury, irrespective of apparent purpose. Code the act only, never the method, and assess risk.
bh.self-harm.cw: Hurting yourself on purpose, often to cope with feelings that seem too much.
bh.self-harm.ex: Hurting oneself after an argument to make overwhelming feelings stop.

bh.aggression.def: Hostile acts toward people or property, such as shouting, threatening, hitting or breaking things, often driven by anger or perceived threat.
bh.aggression.cw: Shouting, threatening, hitting or breaking things when angry.
bh.aggression.ex: Shouting at a partner and slamming doors after feeling criticized.

bh.impulsive-risk-taking.def: Acting quickly without weighing consequences, such as impulsive spending, reckless driving, unsafe sex or gambling, often under strong emotion.
bh.impulsive-risk-taking.cw: Doing risky things on the spur of the moment that you later regret.
bh.impulsive-risk-taking.ex: Spending a month's rent online during a sleepless night.

bh.ascent-behaviors.def: Actions that increase activation, such as taking on many projects, cutting sleep or seeking stimulation, which can escalate toward hypomania.
bh.ascent-behaviors.cw: Pushing yourself to go faster and do more, which can tip you into feeling too high.
bh.ascent-behaviors.ex: Staying up all night starting three new business plans.

bh.appeasing.def: Specific acts of giving in to others against one's own wishes, such as agreeing, over-apologizing or taking on requests, to avoid disapproval.
bh.appeasing.cw: Saying yes, apologizing or going along with others when you really want to say no.
bh.appeasing.ex: Agreeing to cover a colleague's shift despite being exhausted.

bh.self-silencing.def: Keeping opinions, needs, feelings or limits unspoken in a situation, to avoid conflict, rejection or burdening others.
bh.self-silencing.cw: Keeping quiet about what you think or need, so you do not upset anyone.
bh.self-silencing.ex: Saying nothing when a friend repeatedly cancels plans at the last minute.

bh.overworking.def: Working excessive hours or without breaks, often driven by fear of failure or to avoid feelings, at the cost of rest and relationships.
bh.overworking.cw: Working so much that rest, sleep and people you care about get squeezed out.
bh.overworking.ex: Answering work emails until 1 a.m. every night.

bh.redoing-and-overcorrecting.def: Repeatedly checking, rewriting or redoing tasks to meet perfectionistic standards, often taking far longer than needed.
bh.redoing-and-overcorrecting.cw: Going over your work again and again because it never feels good enough.
bh.redoing-and-overcorrecting.ex: Rewriting a two-line email ten times before sending.

bh.excess-time-in-bed.def: Going to bed early, staying in bed late or lying awake for long periods, trying to catch up on lost sleep.
bh.excess-time-in-bed.cw: Spending lots of extra time in bed hoping to get more sleep.
bh.excess-time-in-bed.ex: Going to bed at 9 p.m. after a bad night, then lying awake for hours.

bh.daytime-napping.def: Napping or dozing during the day or evening, which reduces sleep drive at night.
bh.daytime-napping.cw: Taking naps or dozing in the day, which can make night sleep harder.
bh.daytime-napping.ex: Dozing on the couch for two hours in the early evening.

bh.irregular-sleep-schedule.def: Large night-to-night variation in bedtime and rise time, including sleeping in on weekends, which disrupts the body clock.
bh.irregular-sleep-schedule.cw: Going to bed and getting up at very different times from day to day.
bh.irregular-sleep-schedule.ex: Rising at 6 a.m. on weekdays and at noon on weekends.

bh.non-sleep-activities-in-bed.def: Working, using screens or staying in bed while wide awake, which weakens the learned link between bed and sleep.
bh.non-sleep-activities-in-bed.cw: Using your bed for screens, work or lying awake, so bed stops meaning sleep.
bh.non-sleep-activities-in-bed.ex: Answering emails on a laptop in bed until midnight.

bh.clock-monitoring.def: Repeatedly checking the time or a sleep tracker during the night, which raises arousal and worry about lost sleep.
bh.clock-monitoring.cw: Checking the clock or sleep tracker during the night and counting the hours left.
bh.clock-monitoring.ex: Checking the clock every 20 minutes from 2 a.m.

bh.movement-avoidance.def: Avoiding or guarding physical activities and movements expected to cause pain or reinjury, which leads to disuse and disability.
bh.movement-avoidance.cw: Not doing movements or activities because I'm afraid they'll hurt or harm me.
bh.movement-avoidance.ex: Stops picking up the grandchildren since the back pain started.

bh.loss-reminder-avoidance.def: Staying away from places, objects, people, conversations and memories linked to the deceased or the death.
bh.loss-reminder-avoidance.cw: Staying away from anything that reminds me of the person who died.
bh.loss-reminder-avoidance.ex: Takes a long detour so as not to pass the hospital; avoids the cemetery.

bh.pain-overactivity.def: Doing far more than usual when pain is lower, or persisting despite rising pain, which often triggers a flare and enforced rest.
bh.pain-overactivity.cw: Overdoing it when I feel better, then paying for it.
bh.pain-overactivity.ex: Mows the whole lawn and digs the beds on a low-pain morning, then cannot move the next day.

bs.racing-heart.def: Awareness of a fast, forceful or irregular heartbeat; a panic attack symptom often misread as a heart attack.
bs.racing-heart.cw: My heart racing, pounding or skipping a beat.
bs.racing-heart.ex: Heart pounding while waiting to give a toast: "Something's wrong with my heart."

bs.breathlessness.def: Sensation of not getting enough air or of smothering, often with fast, shallow breathing.
bs.breathlessness.cw: Like I can't get enough air in.
bs.breathlessness.ex: On a crowded train: "I'm going to suffocate."

bs.choking.def: Feeling of throat constriction or a lump that makes swallowing or speaking feel hard; occurs in fear and in sadness.
bs.choking.cw: A tight throat or lump that makes it hard to swallow.
bs.choking.ex: Lump in my throat when I tried to speak at the funeral.

bs.chest-tightness.def: Tightness, pressure or pain in the chest during arousal; new or unexplained chest pain needs medical assessment first.
bs.chest-tightness.cw: My chest feels tight, heavy or painful.
bs.chest-tightness.ex: Band of pressure across my chest during an argument.

bs.dizziness.def: Feeling unsteady, lightheaded or about to faint; in panic often misread as a sign of imminent collapse.
bs.dizziness.cw: Lightheaded or wobbly, like I might pass out.
bs.dizziness.ex: Dizzy in the shopping mall: "I'm going to collapse."

bs.jelly-legs.def: Sensation of weakness or wobbliness in the legs, often feared as a sign of fainting or collapse.
bs.jelly-legs.cw: My legs feel weak, like they might give way.
bs.jelly-legs.ex: Legs like jelly walking up to the podium.

bs.trembling.def: Visible or felt shaking of hands, legs, body or voice during anxiety or strong emotion.
bs.trembling.ex: Hands shaking while signing my name in front of the clerk.

bs.sweating.def: Increased sweating, especially palms, face or underarms, during anxiety; often monitored and hidden in social anxiety.
bs.sweating.cw: Sweaty hands or face when I'm stressed.
bs.sweating.ex: Sweaty palms before shaking hands at the interview.

bs.hot-cold-flushes.def: Sudden waves of heat or cold through the body during anxiety or panic.
bs.hot-cold-flushes.cw: Suddenly going hot or cold all over.
bs.hot-cold-flushes.ex: A wave of heat then chills in the doctor's waiting room.

bs.tingling.def: Pins and needles or numbness, often in hands, feet or around the mouth, especially with fast breathing.
bs.tingling.cw: Pins and needles or numb patches, often in hands or face.
bs.tingling.ex: Tingling fingers during a panic attack: "I'm having a stroke."

bs.dry-mouth.def: Dry, sticky mouth from reduced saliva during anxious arousal; can make speaking feel harder.
bs.dry-mouth.cw: My mouth goes dry when I'm nervous.
bs.dry-mouth.ex: Mouth so dry I kept sipping water during my presentation.

bs.blushing.def: Visible reddening of face or neck in social situations; a feared, closely monitored symptom in social anxiety.
bs.blushing.cw: My face going red in front of people.
bs.blushing.ex: Blushing when asked a question in class: "Everyone can see I'm anxious."

bs.startle.def: Exaggerated startle to sudden noises or movement; a hyperarousal sign after trauma and in anxiety.
bs.startle.cw: Jumping out of my skin at sudden noises.
bs.startle.ex: Leaping up when a door slammed down the hall.

bs.muscle-tension.def: Sustained tightening of muscles, often in the neck, shoulders, jaw or back; a core feature of generalized anxiety.
bs.muscle-tension.cw: Tight, tense muscles, often in my neck or shoulders.
bs.muscle-tension.ex: Shoulders up by my ears by the end of the workday.

bs.aches-and-pains.def: Headaches, muscle aches or soreness accompanying chronic tension, low mood or poor sleep; medical causes should be ruled out.
bs.aches-and-pains.ex: Tension headache every afternoon during exam week.

bs.restlessness.def: Physical restlessness or feeling keyed up and unable to settle; a criterion symptom of generalized anxiety disorder.
bs.restlessness.cw: Fidgety and keyed up, unable to sit still.
bs.restlessness.ex: Pacing the kitchen waiting for test results.

bs.butterflies.def: Fluttering, churning or knotted feeling in the stomach during nervous anticipation.
bs.butterflies.cw: Butterflies or a knot in my stomach.
bs.butterflies.ex: Stomach churning on the drive to my first day at a new job.

bs.nausea.def: Queasy, sick feeling, sometimes with gagging or retching; occurs in anxiety, panic and disgust.
bs.nausea.cw: Feeling sick to my stomach, like I might throw up.
bs.nausea.ex: Queasy before every flight: "I'll be sick in front of everyone."

bs.toilet-urgency.def: Sudden urge to empty bowel or bladder under stress, which can lead to avoiding places far from toilets.
bs.toilet-urgency.cw: Suddenly needing the bathroom urgently when I'm stressed.
bs.toilet-urgency.ex: Needing the toilet three times before leaving for the bus.

bs.stomach-pain.def: Ache, cramp or sinking sensation in the gut during stress, dread, shame or envy.
bs.stomach-pain.cw: An ache or sinking feeling in my stomach.
bs.stomach-pain.ex: Sinking feeling in my gut when the boss's email arrived.

bs.fatigue.def: Persistent physical or mental tiredness and lack of energy not relieved by rest; distinct from sleepiness.
bs.fatigue.cw: Drained and out of energy, even after resting.
bs.fatigue.ex: Too tired to shower after a full night in bed.

bs.heaviness.def: Heavy, leaden feeling in the arms or legs; termed leaden paralysis in depression with atypical features.
bs.heaviness.cw: My arms and legs feel as heavy as lead.
bs.heaviness.ex: Legs too heavy to get off the sofa all afternoon.

bs.slowed-down.def: Felt slowing of movement, speech or thinking; termed psychomotor retardation when observable by others.
bs.slowed-down.cw: Everything feels slow, like I'm moving in slow motion.
bs.slowed-down.ex: Took an hour to get dressed this morning.

bs.bedtime-arousal.def: Physical and mental arousal at bedtime that blocks sleep onset despite tiredness; central to cognitive models of insomnia.
bs.bedtime-arousal.cw: Tired but wired in bed, my body and mind won't switch off.
bs.bedtime-arousal.ex: Lying awake at 1 a.m., heart thumping: "I'll be useless tomorrow."

bs.daytime-sleepiness.def: Tendency to doze or fall asleep during the day; differs from fatigue and can signal sleep loss or a sleep disorder.
bs.daytime-sleepiness.cw: Struggling to keep my eyes open in the day.

bs.unrefreshing-sleep.def: Waking feeling unrested or unrecovered despite adequate time asleep.
bs.unrefreshing-sleep.cw: Waking up feeling like I haven't slept.
bs.unrefreshing-sleep.ex: Eight hours in bed and I still woke up exhausted.

bs.night-panic.def: Waking abruptly from sleep in a surge of panic sensations, not caused by a nightmare; common in panic disorder.
bs.night-panic.cw: Jolting awake at night with my heart racing and full of fear.
bs.night-panic.ex: Woke at 3 a.m. gasping with my heart pounding, no dream I could remember.

bs.derealization.def: Surroundings feel unreal, distant, dreamlike or visually distorted, while the person knows this is not literally so.
bs.derealization.cw: The world looks unreal or far away, like a dream or a film.
bs.derealization.ex: In the busy store everything looked flat and fake: "I'm going crazy."

bs.depersonalization.def: Feeling detached from one's own body, thoughts, feelings or actions, as if an outside observer, while knowing this is not literally so.
bs.depersonalization.cw: Disconnected from myself, like I'm watching from outside my body.
bs.depersonalization.ex: Talking at work but feeling like a robot watching myself speak.

bs.blanking-out.def: Blank, absent state in which attention drifts away from the present and time passes unnoticed; may be dissociative under stress.
bs.blanking-out.cw: Spacing out or going blank, and missing what's happening.
bs.blanking-out.ex: During the argument I went blank and missed the last ten minutes.

bs.freeze.def: Sudden inability to move or speak under extreme threat or trauma reminders; an automatic defensive response, not a choice.
bs.freeze.cw: Frozen, unable to move or speak, even though I wanted to.
bs.freeze.ex: When he shouted I froze and couldn't say a word.

bs.heat-rising.def: Heat surging into the face, neck or chest as anger builds; an early warning cue in anger management.
bs.heat-rising.cw: Heat building in my face and chest when I'm getting angry.
bs.heat-rising.ex: Face burning as the driver cut in front of me.

bs.clenching.def: Tightening of the jaw, hands or arms as the body readies to confront; a useful early anger cue.
bs.clenching.cw: Gritting my teeth or balling my fists.
bs.clenching.ex: Fists clenched under the table while my father criticized me.

bs.about-to-explode.def: Mounting internal pressure and energy with urges to hit, shout or lash out; signals rising risk of aggression.
bs.about-to-explode.cw: Like I'm about to explode or lose it.
bs.about-to-explode.ex: Felt like I'd burst if he said one more word, so I walked out.

bs.hunger.def: Strong physical hunger, often after long gaps or dietary restriction, which raises vulnerability to binge eating.
bs.hunger.cw: So hungry I can't think about anything else.
bs.hunger.ex: Skipped breakfast and lunch, ravenous by 4 p.m., then binged.

bs.fullness.def: Uncomfortable stomach fullness or bloating after eating; common when undereating is reversed and often misread as weight gain.
bs.fullness.cw: Uncomfortably full or bloated after eating.
bs.fullness.ex: Bloated after a normal lunch: "I've gained weight already."

bs.feeling-fat.def: Experience of feeling fat that often relabels other emotions or body states such as fullness, bloating, sweating or tight clothes.
bs.feeling-fat.cw: Suddenly feeling fat or huge in my body.
bs.feeling-fat.ex: Felt fat all evening after an argument, though nothing about my body had changed.

bs.poor-appetite.def: Reduced desire to eat during low mood, anxiety or grief; marked weight change warrants assessment.
bs.poor-appetite.cw: Not hungry at all, I can't face food.
bs.poor-appetite.ex: Barely ate for a week after the breakup.

bs.tearful.def: Welling up or crying, often with a tight throat; frequent crying spells can accompany depression, grief or overwhelm.
bs.tearful.cw: Close to tears or crying more than usual.
bs.tearful.ex: Welled up in the car after dropping my son at college.

cd.all-or-nothing-thinking.def: Viewing a situation, person or self in only two extreme categories instead of on a continuum, so anything short of perfect counts as failure.
cd.all-or-nothing-thinking.cw: Seeing things as all good or all bad, with nothing in between.
cd.all-or-nothing-thinking.ex: "If I don't get an A, I'm a total failure."

cd.overgeneralization.def: Drawing a sweeping negative conclusion from a single event or a few events, often signaled by words such as always, never or everyone.
cd.overgeneralization.cw: Treating one bad experience as proof that it will always happen.
cd.overgeneralization.ex: "I got turned down again. Nobody will ever want to go out with me."

cd.labeling.def: Attaching a fixed, global, usually harsh label to oneself or others on the basis of particular behaviors, instead of describing the behavior.
cd.labeling.cw: Calling yourself or someone else a name, like loser or idiot, because of one thing.
cd.labeling.ex: "I forgot her birthday. I'm a terrible friend."

cd.mental-filter.def: Attending to one negative detail, or only to the negative aspects of a situation, and judging the whole by them while overlooking the rest.
cd.mental-filter.cw: Focusing on the one thing that went wrong and missing everything that went right.
cd.mental-filter.ex: Ten people praise a talk and one criticizes it; the client thinks only "It went badly."

cd.disqualifying-the-positive.def: Rejecting positive experiences, qualities or feedback as not counting, for example by crediting luck or kindness, so negative beliefs stay intact.
cd.disqualifying-the-positive.cw: Brushing off good things or compliments as flukes that don't really count.
cd.disqualifying-the-positive.ex: "She only said it went well because she was being nice."

cd.magnification-and-minimization.def: Exaggerating the importance of negatives, such as one's mistakes or others' strengths, while shrinking the importance of positives, such as one's own strengths.
cd.magnification-and-minimization.cw: Blowing your mistakes out of proportion while shrinking your strengths and successes.
cd.magnification-and-minimization.ex: "One typo ruined the whole report. Finishing it early means nothing."

cd.jumping-to-conclusions.def: Reaching a negative conclusion without adequate evidence, or despite contrary evidence. Umbrella term for mind reading and fortune telling.
cd.jumping-to-conclusions.cw: Deciding something bad is true before you have the facts.
cd.jumping-to-conclusions.ex: "He hasn't replied to my text. I must have upset him."

cd.mind-reading.def: Assuming you know what others are thinking, usually that they judge you negatively, without checking or considering other possibilities.
cd.mind-reading.cw: Being sure you know what others think of you, without asking.
cd.mind-reading.ex: "Everyone in the meeting thinks I'm boring."

cd.fortune-telling.def: Predicting a negative outcome as if it were certain, or judging a feared outcome far more likely than the evidence suggests.
cd.fortune-telling.cw: Predicting things will go badly and treating the prediction as a fact.
cd.fortune-telling.ex: "I'll freeze in the interview and won't get the job."

cd.emotional-reasoning.def: Taking one's feelings as evidence of how things really are, reasoning that because something feels true, it must be true.
cd.emotional-reasoning.cw: Believing something is true just because it feels true.
cd.emotional-reasoning.ex: "I feel so anxious, something terrible must be about to happen."

cd.catastrophizing.def: Imagining or expecting the worst possible outcome and judging it unbearable, overestimating how severe the consequences of an event would be.
cd.catastrophizing.cw: Jumping to the worst-case scenario and believing it would be a disaster you couldn't survive.
cd.catastrophizing.ex: "If I lose this job, I'll lose the house and end up on the street."

cd.underestimating-coping.def: Underrating one's ability to cope with a feared event and overlooking available help or rescue factors, which magnifies perceived threat.
cd.underestimating-coping.cw: Believing you couldn't handle it if something bad happened, and that no one would help.
cd.underestimating-coping.ex: "If I get anxious at the party, I won't be able to handle it."

cd.should-statements.def: Holding rigid, absolute demands about how oneself, others or the world should or must be. Unmet demands bring guilt, frustration or anger.
cd.should-statements.cw: Having strict rules about how you or others must act, and feeling bad when they're broken.
cd.should-statements.ex: "I should never make mistakes." "He ought to know how I feel."

cd.low-frustration-tolerance.def: Believing that frustration, discomfort or unpleasant emotion is unbearable and must be avoided or ended at once, rather than unpleasant but tolerable.
cd.low-frustration-tolerance.cw: Telling yourself you can't stand feeling uncomfortable or frustrated, even for a short while.
cd.low-frustration-tolerance.ex: "I can't stand waiting. This is unbearable."

cd.personalization.def: Believing you caused, or are the target of, negative events or others' behavior without considering other, more likely explanations.
cd.personalization.cw: Assuming bad things are your fault or about you, when other reasons are more likely.
cd.personalization.ex: "My son failed his test because I'm a bad mother."

cd.blaming.def: Holding other people or circumstances entirely responsible for one's problems or feelings, overlooking one's own part and what one can change.
cd.blaming.cw: Putting all the blame for a problem on someone else, and missing what you can change.
cd.blaming.ex: "My partner is the reason I'm miserable."

cd.hindsight-bias.def: Judging past decisions with knowledge gained only afterward, believing the outcome was foreseeable and preventable at the time. Common in trauma-related guilt.
cd.hindsight-bias.cw: Blaming yourself for not knowing back then what you only found out later.
cd.hindsight-bias.ex: "I should have known he was dangerous and left sooner."

cd.unfair-comparisons.def: Comparing oneself selectively with people who seem better off, or with unrealistic standards, and concluding one is inferior or lacking.
cd.unfair-comparisons.cw: Measuring yourself against people who seem to be doing better and feeling you come up short.
cd.unfair-comparisons.ex: "Everyone my age has a house and kids. I've achieved nothing."

cd.overly-optimistic-thinking.def: Unrealistically positive predictions about time, effort, ability or future motivation that feel good now but lead to delay and less skill use.
cd.overly-optimistic-thinking.cw: Telling yourself a task will be quick or easy later, so you don't start now.
cd.overly-optimistic-thinking.ex: "It'll only take twenty minutes. I can easily start tonight."

cd.permission-giving-thoughts.def: Thoughts that justify putting off a task or giving in to an urge, bringing short-term relief and so reinforcing avoidance.
cd.permission-giving-thoughts.cw: Thoughts that give you a reason to put something off, like 'I'll just do this first.'
cd.permission-giving-thoughts.ex: "I'll feel more like doing it after I check my email."

cs.avoiding-negative-emotion.def: Habitually avoiding, suppressing or numbing unpleasant emotions, and situations that might trigger them, to protect against feared vulnerability.
cs.avoiding-negative-emotion.cw: Doing whatever it takes not to feel upset, sad or scared.
cs.avoiding-negative-emotion.ex: Never talking about feelings and keeping constantly busy after a loss.

cs.perfectionistic-striving.def: Persistently pursuing very high standards and judging self-worth by meeting them, despite costs, to avoid failure or criticism.
cs.perfectionistic-striving.cw: Pushing yourself to be perfect, because anything less feels like failing.
cs.perfectionistic-striving.ex: Spending every weekend polishing reports that already meet the brief.

cs.overpreparation.def: Preparing far beyond what a task requires, to prevent failure, exposure of inadequacy or uncertainty.
cs.overpreparation.cw: Preparing much more than needed so nothing can possibly go wrong.
cs.overpreparation.ex: Scripting every word of a five-minute team update.

cs.overresponsibility.def: Taking excessive responsibility for others' wellbeing and for preventing harm, beyond one's real role or control.
cs.overresponsibility.cw: Feeling it is your job to keep everyone safe and everything on track.
cs.overresponsibility.ex: Checking on adult siblings daily and fixing their problems for them.

cs.avoiding-intimacy.def: Keeping relationships distant, limiting self-disclosure or ending closeness, to avoid rejection, hurt or exposure.
cs.avoiding-intimacy.cw: Keeping people at arm's length so they cannot get close enough to hurt you.
cs.avoiding-intimacy.ex: Ending relationships once they become serious.

cs.seeking-recognition.def: Pursuing achievement, status or admiration to prove worth and offset an underlying sense of inadequacy.
cs.seeking-recognition.cw: Needing to achieve and be admired to feel good enough.
cs.seeking-recognition.ex: Taking on every high-profile project to be seen as the best.

cs.attention-seeking.def: Drawing others' attention through dramatic, emotional or entertaining displays, to secure care, approval or connection.
cs.attention-seeking.cw: Needing to be noticed and finding ways to make people pay attention to you.
cs.attention-seeking.ex: Escalating stories of crises when friends seem distracted.

cs.avoiding-confrontation.def: Habitually avoiding disagreement, criticism or conflict, even when important issues need raising.
cs.avoiding-confrontation.cw: Keeping the peace at any cost and never raising problems with people.
cs.avoiding-confrontation.ex: Never telling a partner about an ongoing hurt, to avoid an argument.

cs.overcontrol.def: Trying to control situations, people and outcomes tightly, leaving little room for others' input, uncertainty or spontaneity.
cs.overcontrol.cw: Needing to be in charge of everything so nothing goes wrong.
cs.overcontrol.ex: Redoing a partner's chores because they were not done "properly".

cs.dependence-on-others.def: Relying on others to decide, protect or do tasks, and presenting as helpless, to cope with feeling incapable or alone.
cs.dependence-on-others.cw: Leaning on others to decide or do things because you feel you cannot manage alone.
cs.dependence-on-others.ex: Asking a parent to call the bank and make every decision.

cs.pleasing-others.def: A lasting pattern of putting others' wishes first and seeking their approval, to avoid rejection or disapproval.
cs.pleasing-others.cw: Always trying to keep people happy with you, even at your own expense.
cs.pleasing-others.ex: Shaping career, clothes and opinions around what others might want.

cs.excessive-self-reliance.def: Refusing or avoiding help and insisting on handling everything alone, to avoid appearing weak, incompetent or indebted.
cs.excessive-self-reliance.cw: Never asking for help, because needing help feels like weakness or failure.
cs.excessive-self-reliance.ex: Struggling for weeks with a task rather than asking a colleague.

cs.hypervigilance-to-others.def: Watching others closely for signs of hostility, rejection or deception, and staying guarded and slow to trust.
cs.hypervigilance-to-others.cw: Always watching people for signs they might hurt, reject or trick you.
cs.hypervigilance-to-others.ex: Rereading a friend's messages for hidden criticism.

cs.self-sacrifice.def: Routinely meeting others' needs at the expense of one's own, to avoid guilt or causing others pain.
cs.self-sacrifice.cw: Always putting other people's needs before your own, even when it costs you.
cs.self-sacrifice.ex: Caring for relatives every evening while one's own health suffers.

cs.avoiding-challenges.def: Steering away from new tasks, goals or opportunities where failure or inadequacy might be exposed.
cs.avoiding-challenges.cw: Not trying new or hard things in case you fail.
cs.avoiding-challenges.ex: Not applying for a promotion despite encouragement.

cs.asserting-superiority.def: Acting superior, entitled, dominant or critical of others, to ward off underlying feelings of inferiority or vulnerability.
cs.asserting-superiority.cw: Putting others down or acting above them so you never feel small.

cs.rigid-rule-following.def: Relying on strict rules, routines, lists and order to manage uncertainty and avoid mistakes.
cs.rigid-rule-following.cw: Sticking tightly to rules and routines, and feeling uneasy when things change.
cs.rigid-rule-following.ex: Refusing any change to a weekly schedule, even for a celebration.

cs.concealing-vulnerability.def: Hiding perceived flaws, needs or true feelings behind a competent or cheerful front, to avoid rejection or judgment.
cs.concealing-vulnerability.cw: Hiding your real self or struggles behind a front so no one sees weakness.
cs.concealing-vulnerability.ex: Always appearing upbeat at work while privately struggling.

cs.problem-solving.def: Defining a problem, generating options, weighing them, choosing and trying one, then reviewing the result.
cs.problem-solving.cw: Breaking a problem into steps and working through options to sort it out.
cs.problem-solving.ex: Listing three ways to handle rent arrears, then calling the landlord.

cs.seeking-emotional-support.def: Turning to trusted people for comfort, understanding or a chance to talk feelings through.
cs.seeking-emotional-support.cw: Talking to someone you trust about how you feel.
cs.seeking-emotional-support.ex: Calling a friend after a hard day to talk it through.

cs.seeking-practical-help.def: Asking others for advice, information or practical assistance with a problem.
cs.seeking-practical-help.cw: Asking people for advice or hands-on help when you need it.
cs.seeking-practical-help.ex: Asking a colleague to show how to use new software.

cs.self-soothing.def: Using comforting sensory or caring actions, such as warmth, music or gentle touch, to calm distress kindly.
cs.self-soothing.cw: Doing gentle, comforting things for yourself when you are upset.
cs.self-soothing.ex: Taking a warm bath with calming music after a panic attack.

cs.acceptance.def: Allowing unwanted thoughts, feelings and unchangeable realities to be present without struggle, while still choosing helpful action.
cs.acceptance.cw: Letting feelings or facts be there without fighting them, so you can move forward.
cs.acceptance.ex: Making room for grief while still going to work.

cs.balanced-thinking.def: Deliberately weighing the evidence and generating a more balanced or helpful view of a situation.
cs.balanced-thinking.cw: Stepping back to look at the whole picture and find a fairer way to see things.
cs.balanced-thinking.ex: "One mistake does not cancel years of good work."

cs.self-compassion.def: Responding to one's own suffering or mistakes with warmth, understanding and encouragement rather than criticism.
cs.self-compassion.cw: Treating yourself with the kindness you would show a good friend.
cs.self-compassion.ex: "Anyone would struggle with this; I am doing my best."

cs.mindful-awareness.def: Noticing thoughts, feelings and sensations in the present moment as passing events, without judging or acting on them.
cs.mindful-awareness.cw: Noticing thoughts and feelings as they come and go without getting caught up in them.
cs.mindful-awareness.ex: Noticing "I am having the thought that I will fail" and returning to the task.

cs.calming-the-body.def: Using slow breathing, muscle relaxation or similar methods to lower physical arousal, used flexibly rather than as a safety behavior.
cs.calming-the-body.cw: Using slow breathing or relaxing your muscles to settle your body.
cs.calming-the-body.ex: Doing slow breathing for five minutes before a hard conversation.

cs.healthy-distraction.def: Briefly and deliberately shifting attention to absorbing activities to get through acute distress, then returning to the problem.
cs.healthy-distraction.cw: Doing something absorbing for a while to get through a hard moment.
cs.healthy-distraction.ex: Doing a puzzle for 20 minutes until an urge to drink passes.

cs.physical-activity.def: Using exercise or movement in moderation to lift mood, reduce tension and support sleep.
cs.physical-activity.cw: Moving your body, like walking or dancing, to help your mood and stress.
cs.physical-activity.ex: Walking for 20 minutes at lunch on low days.

cs.values-based-action.def: Choosing and taking actions guided by personal values, even when mood or motivation is low.
cs.values-based-action.cw: Doing things that matter to you, even when you do not feel like it.
cs.values-based-action.ex: Attending a child's school event despite low energy.

cs.assertive-communication.def: Clearly and respectfully stating needs, opinions, requests or refusals while considering the other person.
cs.assertive-communication.cw: Saying what you need, or saying no, clearly and kindly.
cs.assertive-communication.ex: "I cannot take this on this week, but I can help next Monday."

cs.opposite-action.def: Acting opposite to an emotion's action urge when the emotion does not fit the facts or acting on it would not help.
cs.opposite-action.cw: Doing the opposite of what a feeling urges, when acting on it would not help.
cs.opposite-action.ex: Calling a friend when sadness urges hiding at home.

cs.urge-surfing.def: Observing a craving or urge rise, peak and fall like a wave, without acting on it.
cs.urge-surfing.cw: Riding out an urge like a wave until it passes, without giving in.
cs.urge-surfing.ex: Noticing the urge to binge, rating it, and watching it fade over 20 minutes.

cs.expressive-writing.def: Putting thoughts and feelings about stressful events into words, in writing or speech, to make sense of them.
cs.expressive-writing.cw: Writing or talking about what happened and how you feel, to make sense of it.
cs.expressive-writing.ex: Writing for 15 minutes about a difficult week.

cs.spiritual-coping.def: Drawing on religious or spiritual beliefs, practices or community for comfort, meaning or guidance.
cs.spiritual-coping.cw: Finding strength or comfort in your faith, prayer or spiritual practice.
cs.spiritual-coping.ex: Praying and attending services for support after a bereavement.

cb.helpless.def: Umbrella self-belief of being ineffective: unable to get things done, protect oneself, or measure up to others.
cb.helpless.cw: Deep down I feel I can't cope or handle things.
cb.helpless.ex: "I can't cope with any of this."

cb.incompetent.def: Belief that one lacks the basic ability to get things done or handle responsibilities, regardless of effort.
cb.incompetent.cw: I'm useless; I can't do things properly.
cb.incompetent.ex: "I'll mess this up like I mess everything up."

cb.needy.def: Belief that one is weak and cannot function, decide or manage daily life without substantial help from others.
cb.needy.cw: I can't manage on my own; I need someone to look after me.
cb.needy.ex: "I couldn't survive if my partner left."

cb.vulnerable.def: Belief that one is weak and unable to protect oneself, so harm, illness or catastrophe is likely.
cb.vulnerable.cw: I can't protect myself; something bad is bound to happen to me.
cb.vulnerable.ex: "If something goes wrong, I won't be able to handle it and I'll get hurt."

cb.powerless.def: Belief that one has no control over one's life or oneself, and is stuck or trapped with no way out.
cb.powerless.cw: I have no control; I'm trapped and nothing I do changes anything.
cb.powerless.ex: "I'm stuck in this situation and there's nothing I can do."

cb.failure.def: Global judgment that one has failed in life or in important roles, drawn from falling short in achievement.
cb.failure.cw: I'm a failure; I've messed up my life.
cb.failure.ex: "I'm unemployed and divorced. I'm a total failure."

cb.inferior.def: Belief that one is less capable or less adequate than other people, reached by comparing oneself with them.
cb.inferior.cw: Everyone else is better than me.
cb.inferior.ex: "Everyone at work is smarter and more capable than me."

cb.not-good-enough.def: Belief that one never meets the required standard in achievement or performance, however much one does.
cb.not-good-enough.cw: Whatever I do, it's never good enough.
cb.not-good-enough.ex: "I got a B. I'm just not good enough."

cb.unlovable.def: Umbrella self-belief that one lacks the qualities that would make others love, want or care about one.
cb.unlovable.cw: Deep down I feel nobody could really love me.
cb.unlovable.ex: "No one could ever love someone like me."

cb.unlikeable.def: Belief that one is socially dull or disagreeable, with nothing to offer, so others will not like or choose one.
cb.unlikeable.cw: People find me boring; I've got nothing to offer.
cb.unlikeable.ex: "Nobody wants to talk to me at parties."

cb.unwanted.def: Belief that one does not matter to others and is not wanted, valued or cared for.
cb.unwanted.ex: "If I disappeared, no one would even notice."

cb.unattractive.def: Belief that one is physically or sexually undesirable, so others will find one unappealing.
cb.unattractive.cw: I'm ugly; no one would find me attractive.
cb.unattractive.ex: "No one would ever want to date me looking like this."

cb.different.def: Belief that one is fundamentally different from other people and does not fit in or belong to any group.
cb.different.cw: I'm different from everyone; I don't fit in anywhere.

cb.defective.def: Belief that something is basically wrong with one, a hidden flaw that would cause rejection if others saw it.
cb.defective.cw: There's something wrong with me, and if people saw it they'd reject me.
cb.defective.ex: "There's something wrong with me that other people don't have."

cb.bound-to-be-rejected.def: Belief that, because of who one is, others will inevitably reject or abandon one, leaving one alone.
cb.bound-to-be-rejected.cw: Sooner or later everyone will leave me, and I'll end up alone.
cb.bound-to-be-rejected.ex: "He'll get bored of me and leave, like everyone does."

cb.worthless.def: Umbrella self-belief that one has no value as a person, or is morally bad, unacceptable or undeserving.
cb.worthless.cw: Deep down I feel I'm worthless as a person.
cb.worthless.ex: "I'm worthless. I'm a waste of space."

cb.bad.def: Belief that one is morally bad, wicked or sinful at the core, not just someone who has done wrong things.
cb.bad.cw: I'm a bad person deep down.
cb.bad.ex: "Good people don't do what I did. I'm rotten inside."

cb.dangerous.def: Belief that one is harmful, toxic or evil and a threat to others; often found behind harm-related obsessions.
cb.dangerous.cw: There's something evil or toxic in me that could hurt people.
cb.dangerous.ex: "Maybe I'm the kind of person who could hurt a child."

cb.crazy.def: Belief that one is mentally unbalanced, abnormal or going mad, often taken as confirmed by one's symptoms.
cb.crazy.cw: I'm crazy; my mind isn't normal.
cb.crazy.ex: "Normal people don't have thoughts like mine. I must be crazy."

cb.undeserving.def: Belief that one does not deserve care, happiness or good things, at the extreme not deserving to live; prompts risk assessment.
cb.undeserving.ex: "Why would I treat myself? I don't deserve it."

cb.effective.def: Adaptive self-belief that one is reasonably competent, in control and able to cope, with ordinary strengths and weaknesses.
cb.effective.cw: I can handle most things reasonably well.
cb.effective.ex: "I'm not perfect, but I can usually cope."

cb.lovable.def: Adaptive self-belief that one is reasonably likeable, wanted and good enough to be loved, and unlikely to end up alone.
cb.lovable.cw: People can like and love me as I am.
cb.lovable.ex: "My friends enjoy my company, even when I'm quiet."

cb.worthwhile.def: Adaptive self-belief that one is reasonably worthwhile, acceptable and good as a person, despite mistakes.
cb.worthwhile.cw: I'm an okay person who has value, even when I get things wrong.
cb.worthwhile.ex: "I made a mistake, but I'm still a decent person."

cb.others-untrustworthy.def: Belief that other people will hurt, deceive, humiliate or exploit one if given the chance.
cb.others-untrustworthy.cw: People can't be trusted; they'll hurt or use me if I let them.
cb.others-untrustworthy.ex: "If I let my guard down, people will take advantage."

cb.others-critical.def: Belief that other people are quick to criticize, judge or reject, and are watching for one's faults.
cb.others-critical.cw: People are judgmental and always looking for my faults.
cb.others-critical.ex: "Everyone in the meeting will notice I'm nervous and judge me."

cb.others-uncaring.def: Belief that other people will not give care, understanding or support when one needs it.
cb.others-uncaring.cw: Nobody really cares; I can't expect support from anyone.
cb.others-uncaring.ex: "There's no point telling anyone. They won't care."

cb.others-unreliable.def: Belief that other people are inconsistent and will let one down or leave, so relationships cannot be counted on.
cb.others-unreliable.cw: People always let you down or leave in the end.
cb.others-unreliable.ex: "Everyone leaves eventually, so why get close?"

cb.others-controlling.def: Belief that other people will dominate, control or intrude on one, so independence must be guarded.
cb.others-controlling.cw: If I let people close, they'll try to control me.
cb.others-controlling.ex: "If I tell my boss my plans, she'll take over."

cb.others-incompetent.def: Belief that other people are careless, irresponsible or incompetent, so one must check or do things oneself.
cb.others-incompetent.cw: Other people are careless; if I want it done right, I do it myself.
cb.others-incompetent.ex: "I can't delegate this. They'll only get it wrong."

cb.others-inferior.def: Belief that other people are weaker, lesser or there to be used, linked to entitlement in some personality presentations.
cb.others-inferior.cw: Most people just aren't on my level.
cb.others-inferior.ex: "Rules are for ordinary people, not for me."

cb.world-dangerous.def: Belief that the world is full of threat, so harm can strike at any time and constant vigilance is needed.
cb.world-dangerous.cw: The world is a dangerous place; nowhere is really safe.
cb.world-dangerous.ex: "Since the attack, I know anything can happen to anyone, anywhere."

cb.world-unpredictable.def: Belief that events are chaotic and uncontrollable, so nothing can be relied on or planned for.
cb.world-unpredictable.cw: Anything can happen; you can never count on things staying stable.
cb.world-unpredictable.ex: "You can lose everything overnight, so why plan?"

cb.world-unfair.def: Belief that the world is unjust, that effort goes unrewarded, and that one is treated worse than one deserves.
cb.world-unfair.cw: Life is unfair; whatever I do, I get a raw deal.
cb.world-unfair.ex: "Other people get the breaks. I never do."

cb.world-demanding.def: Belief that life makes excessive demands and sets obstacles one cannot overcome; the world element of Beck's depressive cognitive triad.
cb.world-demanding.cw: Life is just too hard; everything is an uphill battle.
cb.world-demanding.ex: "Every single thing is a struggle. It's too much."

cb.future-hopeless.def: Belief that things will never improve and one's problems are permanent; the future element of Beck's cognitive triad. Prompts risk assessment.
cb.future-hopeless.cw: Things will never get better for me.
cb.future-hopeless.ex: "It's always going to be like this. There's no point."

cb.future-threatening.def: Belief that the future holds likely danger or catastrophe, so one must anticipate and prepare for the worst.
cb.future-threatening.cw: Something bad is coming, and I need to be ready for it.
cb.future-threatening.ex: "What if I lose my job and we lose the house?"

cb.future-ruined.def: Belief that one's life has been permanently damaged and a normal future is lost; common after trauma.
cb.future-ruined.cw: My life is ruined; I'll never have a normal future.
cb.future-ruined.ex: "After what happened, I'll never have a normal life again."

em.anxious.def: Tense, uneasy apprehension about a possible future threat or uncertain outcome; anticipatory and often diffuse rather than tied to present danger.
em.anxious.cw: Nervous or uneasy, expecting that something bad might happen.
em.anxious.ex: The night before a job interview: "I'll freeze and they'll think I'm useless." Anxious 70.

em.afraid.def: Alarm in response to a threat perceived as present or imminent, preparing the body to fight, flee or freeze.
em.afraid.cw: Scared, as if the danger is right here, right now.
em.afraid.ex: A dog runs toward me barking. Afraid 90.

em.panicky.def: Abrupt surge of intense fear peaking within minutes, usually with strong bodily sensations and fears of dying, collapsing or losing control.
em.panicky.cw: A sudden rush of terror, often with a racing heart and a sense that something awful is happening.
em.panicky.ex: In the supermarket queue: "I'm having a heart attack." Panicky 95.

em.dread.def: Heavy, anticipatory fear of a specific upcoming event that feels unavoidable and bad.
em.dread.cw: A heavy sense that something bad is coming and I can't stop it.
em.dread.ex: All Sunday evening before Monday's meeting with my manager. Dread 80.

em.overwhelmed.def: Sense that demands or emotions exceed one's resources to cope, often with agitation, paralysis or shutting down.
em.overwhelmed.cw: Too much at once, more than I can handle.
em.overwhelmed.ex: Opening 40 unread emails on my first day back after sick leave. Overwhelmed 85.

em.suspicious.def: Wary, fearful expectation that others intend harm, deceit or ridicule; common in paranoia, after trauma and in jealousy.
em.suspicious.cw: On guard, as if people might be against me or up to something.
em.suspicious.ex: Two coworkers stop talking as I walk in: "They're plotting against me." Suspicious 70.

em.sad.def: Painful feeling of loss, disappointment or unmet need, usually linked to a specific event and easing with time.
em.sad.cw: Down, low or unhappy about something.
em.sad.ex: After my closest friend moved to another state. Sad 60.

em.depressed.def: Persistent, pervasive low mood across most of the day and many situations, often with low energy and loss of interest.
em.depressed.cw: Low and heavy most of the time, not just about one thing.
em.depressed.ex: Low most days for a month, even on my birthday. Depressed 80.

em.grief.def: Sorrow and yearning after losing a loved person or something deeply valued; comes in waves. Prolonged, impairing grief warrants assessment.
em.grief.cw: Deep sorrow and missing someone or something I have lost.
em.grief.ex: Finding Mom's handwriting on an old birthday card. Grief 90.

em.disappointed.def: Sadness when an outcome falls short of one's hopes or expectations of oneself, others or events.
em.disappointed.cw: Let down because things did not turn out how I hoped.
em.disappointed.ex: My exam grade came back lower than I expected. Disappointed 50.

em.angry.def: Activated feeling in response to a perceived wrong, unfairness, threat or blocked goal, preparing a person to confront or defend.
em.angry.cw: Mad or furious, like something is unfair or wrong.
em.angry.ex: My partner made weekend plans without asking me: "They don't respect me." Angry 75.

em.irritated.def: Low-level, easily triggered anger or impatience; persistent irritability is common in depression, anxiety, mania and poor sleep.
em.irritated.cw: Annoyed, snappy or short-tempered over small things.
em.irritated.ex: The sound of my partner chewing at dinner. Irritated 40.

em.frustrated.def: Anger-related feeling when effort is blocked or progress toward a goal is repeatedly thwarted.
em.frustrated.cw: Fed up because I keep trying and getting nowhere.
em.frustrated.ex: The online form crashed for the third time. Frustrated 65.

em.resentful.def: Lingering, simmering anger about a past or ongoing perceived injustice, often unexpressed and kept alive by going over it.
em.resentful.cw: Bitter about being treated unfairly, and I can't let it go.
em.resentful.ex: Every time my brother mentions the inheritance. Resentful 70.

em.ashamed.def: Painful sense that the whole self is bad, defective or inferior, with urges to hide, withdraw or disappear.
em.ashamed.cw: Feeling bad about who I am and wanting to hide.
em.ashamed.ex: After crying in front of my team: "I'm pathetic." Ashamed 85.

em.embarrassed.def: Brief, lighter discomfort after a public social slip or unwanted attention; less about the core self than shame.
em.embarrassed.cw: Awkward and self-conscious after something goes wrong in front of others.
em.embarrassed.ex: I called my teacher "Mom" in front of the class. Embarrassed 55.

em.humiliated.def: Intense shame from being degraded, mocked or exposed by others, often in public, frequently with anger at those responsible.
em.humiliated.cw: Put down or made to feel small by someone, often in front of others.
em.humiliated.ex: My boss mocked my report in the team meeting. Humiliated 90.

em.guilty.def: Distress about a specific action or omission judged to have caused harm or broken one's own standards, with urges to repair.
em.guilty.cw: Feeling I did something wrong and wanting to put it right.
em.guilty.ex: "I snapped at my son and made him cry." Guilty 70.

em.regretful.def: Sorrow over a past choice or missed chance, wishing it had gone differently, with or without any moral wrongdoing.
em.regretful.cw: Wishing I had done things differently.
em.regretful.ex: "If only I'd taken that job offer." Regretful 60.

em.disgusted.def: Revulsion toward something seen as contaminating, offensive or morally violating, with urges to expel, avoid or wash.
em.disgusted.cw: Revolted or grossed out, wanting to get away from it.
em.disgusted.ex: Touching the door handle of a public restroom. Disgusted 80.

em.self-disgust.def: Disgust directed at one's own body, actions or whole self; associated with later depressive symptoms.
em.self-disgust.cw: Revolted by myself or my body.
em.self-disgust.ex: Catching my reflection after a binge: "I'm repulsive." Self-disgust 75.

em.contaminated.def: Sense of internal dirtiness or pollution arising without physical contact, often after violation, betrayal or unwanted thoughts; drives washing.
em.contaminated.cw: Feeling dirty or unclean inside, even though I haven't touched anything.
em.contaminated.ex: The memory of the assault came back and I needed to shower. Feeling dirty 85.

em.hurt.def: Emotional pain from perceiving that someone important does not value the relationship as much as one wants.
em.hurt.cw: Wounded by something someone close said or did.
em.hurt.ex: My sister forgot my birthday. Hurt 70.

em.rejected.def: Hurt from being excluded, turned down or pushed away by others; may activate fears of being unlovable.
em.rejected.cw: Unwanted or left out by people I care about.
em.rejected.ex: Seeing photos of a party I wasn't invited to. Rejected 80.

em.betrayed.def: Hurt and anger when a trusted person breaks trust, a promise or loyalty.
em.betrayed.cw: Someone I trusted broke that trust.
em.betrayed.ex: Finding out my friend shared my secret. Betrayed 90.

em.lonely.def: Distress at a gap between wanted and actual social connection, in quantity or quality; can occur when surrounded by people.
em.lonely.cw: Alone or cut off, even when people are around.
em.lonely.ex: Eating dinner alone again on a Friday night. Lonely 75.
