ms.oci-r.def: Eighteen-item self-report of OCD symptom distress with six subscales: washing, checking, ordering, obsessing, hoarding and neutralizing; total 0 to 72.
ms.oci-r.cw: Questions about how much different obsessions and compulsions have distressed you in the past month.
ms.oci-r.ex: High checking and obsessing subscales guide the exposure hierarchy.

ms.docs.def: Twenty-item self-report rating severity across four OCD dimensions: contamination, responsibility for harm, unacceptable thoughts, and symmetry; total 0 to 80.
ms.docs.cw: Questions about four common types of obsessions and compulsions and how much they affect you.
ms.docs.ex: Highest score is the unacceptable thoughts dimension, pointing to mental rituals.

ms.si-r.def: Twenty-three-item self-report of hoarding with clutter, difficulty discarding and excessive acquisition subscales.
ms.si-r.cw: Questions about clutter, difficulty letting go of things, and acquiring things.
ms.si-r.ex: Clutter subscale is high; difficulty discarding is the main treatment focus.

ms.ede-q.def: Twenty-eight-item self-report over the past 28 days: 22 items forming restraint, eating, shape and weight concern subscales, plus six behavior frequencies.
ms.ede-q.cw: Questions about eating, body shape and weight concerns, and eating behaviors over the past four weeks.
ms.ede-q.ex: Global score 4.1 with weekly objective binges; shape concern is the highest subscale.

ms.asrs.def: WHO 18-item self-report of DSM ADHD symptom frequency over six months; the first six items (Part A) form the screener.
ms.asrs.cw: Questions about how often attention, organization and restlessness difficulties happen for you.
ms.asrs.ex: Part A screener is positive, so a full ADHD assessment with collateral history is arranged.

ms.caars-2.def: Normed adult ADHD rating scales with self and observer forms (97 items each), short forms and a 12-item ADHD Index, including impairment items.
ms.caars-2.cw: Questions for you and someone who knows you well about attention, activity and impulsivity.
ms.caars-2.ex: Self and partner ratings both elevated on inattention, supporting the diagnostic assessment.

ms.conners-4.def: Normed ADHD rating scales for youth with parent (117 items), teacher (109) and self-report (118) forms, short forms and a 12-item ADHD Index.
ms.conners-4.cw: Questions for you, your parent and teacher about attention, activity and behavior.
ms.conners-4.ex: Parent and teacher forms both elevated on inattention across home and school.

ms.vanderbilt.def: Parent (55 items) and teacher (43 items) ratings of DSM ADHD symptoms, common comorbid symptoms and school and home performance.
ms.vanderbilt.cw: Questions for parents and teachers about a child's attention, behavior and how they are doing.
ms.vanderbilt.ex: Teacher form meets inattentive criteria with impaired classwork; parent form is borderline.

ms.isi.def: Seven-item self-report of insomnia severity, satisfaction, daytime interference, noticeability and distress, each 0 to 4, total 0 to 28.
ms.isi.cw: Seven questions about your sleep problems and how much they affect you.
ms.isi.ex: Score 19 (moderate clinical insomnia) at intake; 7 after CBT-I.

ms.psqi.def: Self-report of sleep quality over the past month: 19 self-rated items forming seven component scores and a global score of 0 to 21.
ms.psqi.cw: Questions about your sleep habits and sleep quality over the past month.
ms.psqi.ex: Global score 12 indicates poor sleep quality, mainly from long sleep latency.

ms.consensus-sleep-diary.def: Standardized daily sleep diary with nine core items (for example bedtime, sleep latency, awakenings, final wake time, quality) used to calculate sleep parameters.
ms.consensus-sleep-diary.cw: A daily record you fill in each morning about when and how you slept.
ms.consensus-sleep-diary.ex: Two weeks of diaries show sleep efficiency of 68%, used to set the sleep window.

ms.audit.def: WHO 10-item screen for hazardous and harmful drinking and dependence, total 0 to 40, with risk zones at 8, 16 and 20.
ms.audit.cw: Ten questions about how much and how often you drink, and its effects.
ms.audit.ex: Score 17 (zone III), so brief intervention plus monitoring and further assessment are offered.

ms.audit-c.def: First three AUDIT items on drinking frequency, typical quantity and heavy episodes, total 0 to 12, used as a brief alcohol screen.
ms.audit-c.cw: Three questions about how often and how much you drink.
ms.audit-c.ex: Positive AUDIT-C prompts the full AUDIT.

ms.dast-10.def: Ten yes or no items on consequences of drug use (excluding alcohol and tobacco) over the past 12 months, total 0 to 10.
ms.dast-10.cw: Ten yes or no questions about drug use and its effects over the past year.
ms.dast-10.ex: Score 6 (substantial level) leads to fuller substance use assessment.

ms.wsas.def: Five-item self-report of impairment attributed to the main problem in work, home management, social leisure, private leisure and relationships, each 0 to 8.
ms.wsas.cw: Five questions about how much your problem affects work, home life, leisure and relationships.
ms.wsas.ex: Score 24 at intake shows marked impairment; 9 at discharge.

ms.core-10.def: Ten-item self-report of general psychological distress over the past week, covering anxiety, depression, functioning and risk; total 0 to 40.
ms.core-10.cw: Ten questions about how you have been feeling and coping over the last week.
ms.core-10.ex: Score drops from 24 to 9, crossing the clinical cutpoint.

ms.ders.def: Thirty-six-item self-report of emotion regulation difficulties: nonacceptance, goals, impulse control, awareness, strategies and clarity.
ms.ders.cw: Questions about how you notice, understand and manage strong emotions.
ms.ders.ex: High impulse and strategies subscales support adding DBT-informed skills.

ms.rrs.def: Twenty-two-item self-report of the tendency to ruminate in response to low mood, with brooding and reflection subscales.
ms.rrs.cw: Questions about what you tend to do and think when you feel down.
ms.rrs.ex: High brooding score supports rumination-focused work.

ms.ors.def: Four visual analog scales rating individual, interpersonal, social and overall wellbeing, total 0 to 40, given at the start of each session.
ms.ors.cw: Four quick lines to mark how you have been doing in different areas of life.
ms.ors.ex: ORS score is below the clinical cutoff and has not improved by session 4, prompting a review.

ms.srs.def: Four visual analog scales rating the session's relationship, goals and topics, approach or method, and overall fit, total 0 to 40.
ms.srs.cw: Four quick lines to tell me how today's session worked for you.
ms.srs.ex: A lower approach rating leads the therapist to ask what would work better next time.

ms.wai-sr.def: Twelve-item client-rated measure of the therapeutic alliance with goal, task and bond subscales, based on Bordin's model.
ms.wai-sr.cw: Questions about how well you and your therapist are working together.
ms.wai-sr.ex: Low task subscale prompts a discussion about how homework is set.

ms.cts-r.def: Twelve-item observer-rated scale of CBT therapist competence, each item 0 to 6, covering structure, relationship and change techniques.
ms.cts-r.cw: A rating of how the therapist delivered CBT in a recorded session, used in training.
ms.cts-r.ex: A supervisor rates a recorded session and identifies guided discovery as the skill to develop.

ms.c-ssrs.def: Structured questions on suicidal ideation, its intensity, preparatory behavior and attempts; the screener asks 2 to 6 questions depending on answers.
ms.c-ssrs.cw: Direct questions about thoughts of suicide and any steps taken, so we can keep you safe.
ms.c-ssrs.ex: Screener positive for recent ideation with intent, so same-day safety planning and escalation follow.

ms.suds.def: Single client rating of current distress or fear from 0 to 100, used to build hierarchies and track within-task change.
ms.suds.cw: A 0 to 100 rating of how upset or anxious you feel right now.
ms.suds.ex: SUDS 75 at the start of exposure and 40 at the end.

ms.goal-based-outcomes.def: Client rates progress toward up to three personally chosen goals on a 0 to 10 scale at intake and review.
ms.goal-based-outcomes.cw: Rating how close you are to each of your own goals, from 0 to 10.
ms.goal-based-outcomes.ex: "Go to school every day" moves from 2 to 7 by session 10.

rk.prior-suicide-attempt.def: Any past self-initiated, potentially injurious act with at least some intent to die, including interrupted and aborted attempts; a key historical risk factor.
rk.prior-suicide-attempt.cw: I have tried to end my life before.
rk.prior-suicide-attempt.ex: Reports one attempt at age 19 and an interrupted attempt two years ago.

rk.history-of-self-harm.def: Past deliberate self-injury without intent to die; it raises later risk of suicide and repeat self-harm and is recorded separately from attempts.
rk.history-of-self-harm.cw: I have hurt myself on purpose before, without wanting to die.
rk.history-of-self-harm.ex: Self-harmed to cope with distress in high school; none in the past year.

rk.family-history-or-exposure-to-suicide.def: Suicide or suicide attempts by a family member, close friend or peer, or living in a community with a recent suicide cluster.
rk.family-history-or-exposure-to-suicide.cw: Someone in my family, or someone close to me, has died by suicide or tried to.
rk.family-history-or-exposure-to-suicide.ex: Mother died by suicide when the client was 12.

rk.childhood-adversity.def: Abuse, neglect, household violence or other serious adversity in childhood, recorded as an enduring background risk factor for suicide.
rk.childhood-adversity.cw: Hard or harmful things happened to me when I was growing up.
rk.childhood-adversity.ex: Physical abuse by a stepparent between ages 8 and 14.

rk.history-of-mental-disorder.def: Past or lifetime depression, bipolar disorder, psychosis, substance use, eating, personality or other mental disorder, or past mental health treatment.
rk.history-of-mental-disorder.cw: I have had mental health problems or treatment in the past.
rk.history-of-mental-disorder.ex: Two previous depressive episodes and one psychiatric admission.

rk.impulsive-or-aggressive-traits.def: A longstanding pattern of acting quickly on urges or reacting aggressively, which can shorten the step from suicidal thought to action.
rk.impulsive-or-aggressive-traits.cw: I tend to act on impulse or lash out before I can think it through.
rk.impulsive-or-aggressive-traits.ex: Long history of sudden outbursts and acting without thinking when upset.

rk.thwarted-belongingness.def: An unmet need to belong: feeling lonely and lacking reciprocally caring relationships, even when other people are around.
rk.thwarted-belongingness.cw: I feel alone, like I don't really belong or matter to anyone.
rk.thwarted-belongingness.ex: "Nobody would even notice if I disappeared."

rk.defeat-or-humiliation.def: A loss, rejection or failure experienced as a crushing defeat or humiliation, often with intense shame; a common trigger for entrapment.
rk.defeat-or-humiliation.cw: I feel humiliated, beaten down, or ashamed after what happened.
rk.defeat-or-humiliation.ex: Feels publicly shamed after being fired in front of colleagues.

rk.substance-use-problem.def: Ongoing harmful or dependent use of alcohol or drugs, which raises risk through disinhibition, low mood and its life consequences.
rk.substance-use-problem.cw: My drinking or drug use has been a problem for a while.
rk.substance-use-problem.ex: Daily heavy drinking for three years, with blackouts.

rk.acute-life-stressor.def: A recent loss or crisis, such as relationship breakdown, bereavement, job or financial loss, or legal trouble, that precipitates or worsens risk.
rk.acute-life-stressor.cw: Something really hard has just happened, like a loss or a crisis.
rk.acute-life-stressor.ex: Partner left last week, and the client faces eviction.

rk.access-to-lethal-means.def: Ready access to means that could be used in a suicide attempt; a modifiable factor addressed by restricting access to lethal means.
rk.access-to-lethal-means.cw: There are things at home I could use to seriously hurt myself.
rk.access-to-lethal-means.ex: Means are kept at home; partner agrees to remove them and keep them elsewhere.

rk.active-psychotic-symptoms.def: Current hallucinations or delusions, especially commands to harm or beliefs of being threatened, that may drive harm to self or others.
rk.active-psychotic-symptoms.cw: I hear voices, or have frightening beliefs, that push me to hurt myself or others.
rk.active-psychotic-symptoms.ex: Hears a voice telling him he must punish himself; believes neighbors are plotting against him.

rk.suicidal-communication.def: Talking, writing or posting about wanting to die or kill oneself; a direct warning sign that calls for prompt risk assessment.
rk.suicidal-communication.cw: I've been talking or writing about wanting to die.
rk.suicidal-communication.ex: Posted online: "I won't be a problem for anyone much longer."

rk.passive-suicidal-ideation.def: Thoughts of wanting to be dead or not wake up, without thoughts of acting to end one's own life.
rk.passive-suicidal-ideation.cw: Sometimes I wish I could go to sleep and not wake up.
rk.passive-suicidal-ideation.ex: "I wouldn't mind if I just didn't wake up tomorrow."

rk.active-suicidal-ideation.def: Thoughts of killing oneself, from nonspecific thoughts to thinking about how, without stated intent to act on them.
rk.active-suicidal-ideation.cw: I've been having thoughts about killing myself.
rk.active-suicidal-ideation.ex: "I keep thinking about ending my life, but I don't plan to do it."

rk.suicidal-intent.def: Some intention to act on suicidal thoughts, as distinct from having the thoughts while clearly not intending to act.
rk.suicidal-intent.cw: Part of me means to act on these thoughts.
rk.suicidal-intent.ex: Says they would act on the thoughts if things do not change soon.

rk.suicide-plan.def: Suicidal intent with some details of a plan worked out; document that a plan exists and its timing, not method specifics.
rk.suicide-plan.cw: I've started working out a plan to end my life.
rk.suicide-plan.ex: Reports a plan and a chosen date; plan reviewed in the confidential risk record.

rk.preparatory-behavior.def: Acts beyond thought or talk that prepare for a suicide attempt, such as obtaining means or searching for ways to end one's life.
rk.preparatory-behavior.cw: I've started getting things ready, or looking up ways to end my life.
rk.preparatory-behavior.ex: Has been searching online for ways to die this week.

rk.final-arrangements.def: Putting affairs in order in anticipation of death: giving away prized possessions, contacting people to say goodbye, or writing a note.
rk.final-arrangements.cw: I've been giving my things away or saying goodbye to people.
rk.final-arrangements.ex: Gave her guitar to a friend and called her sister "to say goodbye."

rk.unbearable-psychological-pain.def: Emotional pain experienced as unbearable or endless, often voiced as wanting the pain to stop rather than wanting to die.
rk.unbearable-psychological-pain.cw: The pain inside feels unbearable, and I just want it to stop.
rk.unbearable-psychological-pain.ex: "I can't take feeling like this anymore."

rk.no-reason-to-live.def: Stating that life has no purpose or that there is nothing left to live for.
rk.no-reason-to-live.cw: I can't see any reason to keep living.

rk.sleep-change.def: Sleeping much more or much less than usual, including new or worsening insomnia, as a near-term warning sign.
rk.sleep-change.cw: My sleep has changed a lot: I hardly sleep, or I sleep all the time.
rk.sleep-change.ex: Sleeping about three hours a night for the past two weeks.

rk.agitation-or-anger.def: New or increased agitation, restlessness, irritability, rage or uncharacteristic aggression, including talk of seeking revenge.
rk.agitation-or-anger.cw: I've been really on edge, restless, or angry lately.
rk.agitation-or-anger.ex: Pacing during the session, snapping at staff, which is unlike him.

rk.sudden-calm.def: An abrupt sense of relief or calm after a period of despair, which may signal a decision to die rather than recovery.
rk.sudden-calm.cw: I suddenly feel calm and settled after feeling so low.
rk.sudden-calm.ex: Appears unusually at peace a day after saying life is unbearable.

rk.reasons-for-living.def: People, plans, beliefs or roles the person names as reasons to stay alive; ask directly and record them in the person's own words.
rk.reasons-for-living.cw: I have people and things that keep me going.
rk.reasons-for-living.ex: "My kids, my dog, and seeing my sister graduate next year."

rk.responsibility-to-others.def: Felt responsibility for children, family or pets, and concern about how one's death would affect them.
rk.responsibility-to-others.cw: I couldn't do that to my kids, my family, or my pets.
rk.responsibility-to-others.ex: "Who would look after my mom if I wasn't here?"

rk.engagement-with-care.def: Consistent access to, and active engagement with, physical and mental health care, including a working relationship with the clinician.
rk.engagement-with-care.cw: I'm connected with care and want to keep working with my treatment team.
rk.engagement-with-care.ex: Attends every session and has a primary care doctor and psychiatrist she trusts.

rk.moral-or-religious-objection.def: Cultural, religious or moral beliefs that suicide is wrong, which the person says would hold them back from acting.
rk.moral-or-religious-objection.cw: My faith or values tell me suicide isn't an option for me.
rk.moral-or-religious-objection.ex: "My faith says it isn't my life to take."

rk.violent-ideation-or-intent.def: Thoughts, urges, fantasies or intentions of seriously harming another person, recorded with their frequency, target and level of intent.
rk.violent-ideation-or-intent.cw: I've been having thoughts or urges about hurting someone else.
rk.violent-ideation-or-intent.ex: Reports daily thoughts of hurting his former manager but denies intent.

rk.threat-to-identifiable-person.def: A serious threat of physical violence against a reasonably identifiable victim, which may trigger duty-to-warn or duty-to-protect obligations under state law.
rk.threat-to-identifiable-person.cw: I've said I'm going to hurt a particular person.
rk.threat-to-identifiable-person.ex: Says he will hurt his ex-partner's new boyfriend this weekend.

rk.history-of-violence.def: Past acts, attempts or credible threats of physical or sexual violence against others; a core historical item in structured violence risk assessment.
rk.history-of-violence.cw: I've hurt other people physically in the past.
rk.history-of-violence.ex: Two assault convictions; last incident five years ago.

rk.violent-attitudes.def: Attitudes that condone, justify or minimize violence, or hostile beliefs that particular people deserve to be harmed.
rk.violent-attitudes.cw: Sometimes I think violence is justified, or that some people deserve to get hurt.
rk.violent-attitudes.ex: "If someone disrespects you, they've earned a beating."

rk.intimate-partner-violence-perpetratio.def: Using physical or sexual violence, stalking, or psychological aggression to harm or control a current or former partner.
rk.intimate-partner-violence-perpetratio.cw: I've hurt, threatened, or tried to control a partner or an ex.
rk.intimate-partner-violence-perpetratio.ex: Checks partner's phone daily and has pushed her during arguments.

rk.child-maltreatment-concern.def: Reasonable suspicion that a child is experiencing physical, sexual or emotional abuse, neglect, sexual exploitation or abandonment.
rk.child-maltreatment-concern.cw: I'm worried that a child is being hurt or not properly looked after.
rk.child-maltreatment-concern.ex: Client says her partner hits her 6-year-old when he drinks.

rk.domestic-abuse-victimization.def: The client is experiencing violence, sexual coercion, stalking, threats or controlling behavior from a current or former partner or family member.
rk.domestic-abuse-victimization.cw: Someone at home, or an ex, is hurting, threatening, or controlling me.
rk.domestic-abuse-victimization.ex: Partner controls her money and phone and has threatened to take the children.

rk.elder-abuse.def: An intentional act or failure to act that causes or risks harm to an older adult: physical, sexual, emotional, neglect or financial.
rk.elder-abuse.cw: An older person is being hurt, neglected, or taken advantage of by someone.
rk.elder-abuse.ex: Client's son takes her pension and leaves her without food.

rk.abuse-of-adult-at-risk.def: Abuse or neglect of an adult with care and support needs who cannot protect themselves: physical, sexual, psychological, financial, discriminatory or organizational.
rk.abuse-of-adult-at-risk.cw: An adult who relies on others for care is being harmed or taken advantage of.
rk.abuse-of-adult-at-risk.ex: Client's brother with an intellectual disability is locked in his room by a paid caregiver.

rk.self-neglect.def: Inability or unwillingness to meet one's own basic needs for health, hygiene, nutrition, safety or surroundings, to a degree that risks harm.
rk.self-neglect.cw: I haven't been able to look after myself, like eating, washing, or my home.
rk.self-neglect.ex: Not eating regular meals; home without heating; missed medical appointments.

rk.exploitation-or-trafficking.def: Being coerced or deceived into sexual activity, labor, crime or servitude for another person's gain, including trafficking and debt bondage.
rk.exploitation-or-trafficking.cw: Someone is forcing or tricking me into doing things for their benefit.
rk.exploitation-or-trafficking.ex: Teenager is given gifts by older men and pressured to carry drugs.

sit.criticism.def: Receiving, or believing one has received, negative comments, correction or disapproval about one's actions, appearance or character.
sit.criticism.cw: Someone criticizes you, corrects you, or seems to disapprove of you.
sit.criticism.ex: A manager points out errors in a report in front of colleagues.

sit.rejection-or-exclusion.def: Being turned down, left out, ignored or not responded to by others, or noticing signs that one may be unwanted.
sit.rejection-or-exclusion.cw: Someone turns you down, leaves you out, ignores you, or does not reply.
sit.rejection-or-exclusion.ex: Friends post photos from a gathering the client was not invited to.

sit.interpersonal-conflict.def: An argument, disagreement or tense exchange with another person, in person or in writing, including a confrontation the person expects.
sit.interpersonal-conflict.cw: An argument, disagreement or tense moment with someone, or one you expect is coming.
sit.interpersonal-conflict.ex: A partner raises their voice during a disagreement about money.

sit.being-observed.def: Doing an ordinary activity, such as eating, drinking, writing, walking or working, while others can watch.
sit.being-observed.cw: Doing everyday things while other people can see you, like eating, writing or walking past.
sit.being-observed.ex: Signing a form while a bank clerk waits and watches.

sit.social-interaction.def: Conversations and social gatherings, including meeting unfamiliar people, small talk, parties, dates and talking with people in authority.
sit.social-interaction.cw: Talking with people, meeting someone new, parties, dates, or speaking with someone in charge.
sit.social-interaction.ex: Making small talk with coworkers in the lunch line.

sit.public-performance.def: Speaking, presenting, performing or playing sport in front of an audience whose attention is on the person.
sit.public-performance.cw: Speaking, presenting or performing while people watch and listen to you.
sit.public-performance.ex: Giving a toast at a friend's wedding.

sit.praise-or-attention.def: Receiving compliments, positive feedback or public recognition, or otherwise becoming the focus of others' attention.
sit.praise-or-attention.cw: Someone praises or compliments you, or everyone's attention turns to you.
sit.praise-or-attention.ex: Being singled out for thanks at a team meeting.

sit.asserting-needs.def: Situations calling for the person to refuse, request, complain, disagree or set a limit with someone else.
sit.asserting-needs.cw: Times you need to say no, ask for something, complain, or stand up for yourself.
sit.asserting-needs.ex: Needing to return a faulty purchase to a store.

sit.social-comparison.def: Encountering information about other people's achievements, appearance, lifestyles or relationships, in person or online, that invites comparison with oneself.
sit.social-comparison.cw: Seeing how others look, live or succeed, in person or online, and comparing yourself.
sit.social-comparison.ex: Scrolling past a former classmate's promotion announcement.

sit.separation-or-abandonment-cue.def: A close person leaving, being away or unreachable, or showing cues the person reads as signs they may leave.
sit.separation-or-abandonment-cue.cw: Someone close leaves, goes away, is hard to reach, or seems like they might leave.
sit.separation-or-abandonment-cue.ex: A partner is out late and not answering texts.

sit.social-pressure-to-use.def: Being directly offered alcohol or drugs, or being around others who are drinking or using.
sit.social-pressure-to-use.cw: Being offered a drink or drug, or being with people who are drinking or using.
sit.social-pressure-to-use.ex: A friend hands over a beer at a barbecue.

sit.being-alone.def: Time without company, such as evenings, weekends or living alone, especially when the person wants contact with others.
sit.being-alone.cw: Times you are on your own, like evenings or weekends, especially when you want company.
sit.being-alone.ex: Sunday evening alone in the apartment after a partner moved out.

sit.positive-event.def: Celebrations, good news or reaching a valued goal, which can trigger substance use, manic symptoms or discomfort with success.
sit.positive-event.cw: Good things happening, like celebrations, good news, or reaching a goal.
sit.positive-event.ex: Landing a new job and going out to celebrate.

sit.performance-evaluation.def: Situations where performance is formally judged or graded, such as exams, interviews, appraisals, auditions or inspections.
sit.performance-evaluation.cw: Times your work or ability is judged, like exams, interviews, or reviews at work.
sit.performance-evaluation.ex: A driving test booked for Friday morning.

sit.task-start.def: The point of beginning a task, especially one experienced as boring, difficult, ambiguous or unpleasant.
sit.task-start.cw: The moment you need to start something, especially a boring, hard or unclear job.
sit.task-start.ex: Opening the laptop to begin a tax return.

sit.deadline-or-time-pressure.def: An approaching due date, or more tasks and responsibilities than the time or energy available.
sit.deadline-or-time-pressure.cw: A due date is coming up, or there is too much to do in the time you have.
sit.deadline-or-time-pressure.ex: An assignment due tomorrow morning with half still to write.

sit.mistake-or-setback.def: Making an error, failing at something, or falling short of a personal standard or goal.
sit.mistake-or-setback.cw: You make a mistake, something goes wrong, or you fall short of what you hoped.

sit.decision-making.def: Needing to choose between options, especially when outcomes are uncertain or a wrong choice feels costly.
sit.decision-making.cw: Needing to make a choice when you cannot be sure which option is right.
sit.decision-making.ex: Choosing which apartment to rent before the offer expires.

sit.unstructured-time.def: Periods with no planned activity or external structure, such as weekends, holidays, days off work or retirement.
sit.unstructured-time.cw: Stretches of time with nothing planned, like empty weekends or days off.
sit.unstructured-time.ex: A long holiday weekend with no plans.

sit.responsibility-for-harm.def: Situations where the person could cause, or fail to prevent, harm to self or others, such as locking up, driving or cooking.
sit.responsibility-for-harm.cw: Times when you feel something bad could happen if you do not take enough care.
sit.responsibility-for-harm.ex: Being the last to leave the office and setting the alarm.

sit.agoraphobic-situations.def: Places where escape or help may feel hard to get: public transport, open or enclosed spaces, lines, crowds, or outside home alone.
sit.agoraphobic-situations.cw: Places that feel hard to leave or get help in, like buses, crowds, lines or stores.
sit.agoraphobic-situations.ex: Standing in a long checkout line at a busy supermarket.

sit.phobic-stimulus.def: A circumscribed feared object or situation, such as animals, heights, storms, water, blood, injections, flying or enclosed spaces.
sit.phobic-stimulus.cw: A particular thing you fear, like spiders, heights, needles, flying, or small spaces.
sit.phobic-stimulus.ex: Seeing a dog off its leash in the park.

sit.trauma-reminder.def: Sights, sounds, smells, bodily states, places, people, dates or situations that resemble or are linked to a traumatic event.
sit.trauma-reminder.cw: Things that remind you of what happened, like a place, smell, sound, person or date.
sit.trauma-reminder.ex: Hearing screeching brakes years after a car crash.

sit.loss-reminder.def: Dates, places, objects or events that bring to mind a person, relationship or role that has been lost.
sit.loss-reminder.cw: Things that remind you of someone or something you have lost, like anniversaries or belongings.
sit.loss-reminder.ex: The first holiday season after a parent's death.

sit.health-information.def: Encountering information about illness, such as media stories, online symptom content, or a friend or relative becoming ill.
sit.health-information.cw: Hearing or reading about illness, online, in the news, or when someone you know gets sick.
sit.health-information.ex: Reading an article about a celebrity's cancer diagnosis.

sit.medical-appointment-or-test.def: Medical or dental appointments, examinations, procedures, screenings, and waiting for test results.
sit.medical-appointment-or-test.cw: Doctor or dentist visits, medical tests, injections, or waiting for results.
sit.medical-appointment-or-test.ex: Waiting a week for biopsy results.

sit.eating-situation.def: Meals and food-related situations, including eating with others, feared or unplanned foods, buffets and food shopping.
sit.eating-situation.cw: Meals and food situations, like eating with others, feared foods, or food you did not plan.
sit.eating-situation.ex: Being offered cake at an office party.

sit.body-image-cue.def: Situations that draw attention to body shape or weight, such as weighing, mirrors, photographs, tight clothes or seeing others' bodies.
sit.body-image-cue.cw: Things that make you notice your shape or weight, like scales, mirrors, photos, or tight clothes.
sit.body-image-cue.ex: Jeans feeling tight when getting dressed.

sit.bedtime.def: Preparing for sleep, lying in bed trying to sleep, or waking during the night or too early.
sit.bedtime.cw: Getting ready for bed, lying awake, or waking up in the night.
sit.bedtime.ex: Lying in bed at 1 a.m., still awake, with an early meeting.

sit.substance-cue.def: Places, objects, times or people associated with past alcohol or drug use that can trigger cravings.
sit.substance-cue.cw: Places, things, times or people linked to past drinking or drug use.
sit.substance-cue.ex: Walking past the bar where the client used to drink after work.

sit.contamination-cue.def: Contact, or possible contact, with things perceived as dirty, germ-laden, toxic or morally contaminating.
sit.contamination-cue.cw: Touching, or maybe touching, things that feel dirty, germy, toxic or tainted.

sit.uncertainty-or-waiting.def: Situations whose outcome is unknown, ambiguous or unpredictable, including waiting for news or plans not yet confirmed.
sit.uncertainty-or-waiting.cw: Not knowing how something will turn out, or waiting to hear news.
sit.uncertainty-or-waiting.ex: A partner traveling who has not yet confirmed a safe arrival.

sit.change-in-routine.def: Unexpected changes to plans, routines or surroundings, including new places, schedules or people.
sit.change-in-routine.cw: Plans or routines changing, especially without warning, or being somewhere new.
sit.change-in-routine.ex: A class moved to a different room at short notice.

sit.arousal-sensations.def: Noticing bodily sensations of arousal, such as racing heart, breathlessness, dizziness or trembling, which then act as a trigger.
sit.arousal-sensations.cw: Noticing your heart racing, feeling dizzy, short of breath, or shaky.

sit.bodily-change-or-symptom.def: Noticing a new or unexplained bodily change, such as a lump, ache, mark, or altered bodily function.
sit.bodily-change-or-symptom.cw: Noticing something new or odd in your body, like a lump, pain, mark, or change.
sit.bodily-change-or-symptom.ex: Finding a mole that looks darker than before.

sit.fatigue-or-sleep-loss.def: Feeling tired or having slept poorly, which lowers coping and can trigger low mood, irritability, worry or mood episodes.
sit.fatigue-or-sleep-loss.cw: Feeling worn out, or having slept badly.
sit.fatigue-or-sleep-loss.ex: Waking after four hours of broken sleep before a busy day.

sit.hunger-or-dietary-restriction.def: Physical hunger or a period of undereating or strict dieting, which raises the risk of binge eating and food preoccupation.
sit.hunger-or-dietary-restriction.cw: Being very hungry, or having skipped meals or eaten much less than usual.
sit.hunger-or-dietary-restriction.ex: Arriving home at 7 p.m. having eaten nothing since breakfast.

sit.pain-or-illness-flare.def: An increase in pain, a bout of physical illness, or other physical discomfort that acts as a trigger.
sit.pain-or-illness-flare.cw: Pain getting worse, feeling physically ill, or your body feeling off.
sit.pain-or-illness-flare.ex: A back pain flare that cancels weekend plans.

sit.intrusive-thought-or-impulse.def: An unwanted thought, doubt or impulse that pops into mind, often about harm, contamination, sex, religion or mistakes.
sit.intrusive-thought-or-impulse.cw: An unwanted thought, doubt or urge that pops into your head out of nowhere.
sit.intrusive-thought-or-impulse.ex: "What if I left the stove on and the house burns down?"

sit.intrusive-memory.def: An unwanted memory of a past traumatic or painful event coming to mind, spontaneously or when cued.
sit.intrusive-memory.cw: A memory of something painful from the past that comes back when you do not want it.
sit.intrusive-memory.ex: Suddenly recalling an embarrassing moment from a meeting last year.

sit.distressing-mental-image.def: A vivid image of a feared or upsetting scene, real or imagined, such as seeing oneself humiliated, ill or harmed.
sit.distressing-mental-image.cw: A vivid picture in your mind of something upsetting or frightening happening.
sit.distressing-mental-image.ex: Picturing oneself blushing and shaking while everyone stares.

sit.mood-shift.def: Noticing an emotion begin or intensify, such as low mood, anxiety, anger, boredom or excitement, which then acts as a trigger.
sit.mood-shift.cw: Noticing a feeling start or get stronger, like sadness, worry, anger, or boredom.
sit.mood-shift.ex: Feeling a wave of sadness while washing up after dinner.

sit.urge-or-craving.def: Noticing an urge to act, such as to drink, use, binge, check or seek reassurance, which itself prompts further reactions.
sit.urge-or-craving.cw: Noticing a strong pull to do something, like drink, binge, check, or ask for reassurance.
sit.urge-or-craving.ex: A sudden strong craving for a cigarette after morning coffee.

ts.open-question.def: A question that invites an elaborated answer in the client's own words, rather than yes, no, or a single fact.
ts.open-question.cw: A question I can answer in my own words, at whatever length I want.
ts.open-question.ex: "What has the past week been like for you?"

ts.closed-question.def: A question that limits the answer to yes or no, a choice between options, or a specific fact such as a number or rating.
ts.closed-question.cw: A quick question with a short answer, like yes, no, or a number.
ts.closed-question.ex: "Did you try the breathing exercise this week?"

ts.guided-discovery.def: The overall CBT process in which questions, summaries and experiments help the client reach new perspectives through their own observation and reasoning.
ts.guided-discovery.cw: We work things out together, so I discover answers myself instead of being told.
ts.guided-discovery.ex: "How could we find out whether that prediction is true?"

ts.socratic-questioning.def: Padesky's four-stage dialogue of informational questions, empathic listening, summary and synthesizing questions, aimed at guiding discovery rather than changing the client's mind.
ts.socratic-questioning.cw: Thoughtful questions that help me look at my situation from new angles.
ts.socratic-questioning.ex: "What did you notice when you spoke up? ... Putting that together, what does it say about the idea that people will laugh?"

ts.socratic-informational-question.def: Stage 1 of Socratic dialogue: concrete questions, within the client's knowledge, that bring overlooked or unnoticed information into awareness.
ts.socratic-informational-question.cw: Questions that help me notice facts I knew but hadn't been paying attention to.
ts.socratic-informational-question.ex: "Have there been times you expected to be rejected and it turned out differently?"

ts.socratic-empathic-listening.def: Stage 2 of Socratic dialogue: listening closely for the client's meanings, emotional reactions and missing information, and using them to choose the next question.
ts.socratic-empathic-listening.cw: The therapist really listens to what my answers mean to me before asking more.
ts.socratic-empathic-listening.ex: The therapist hears the client stress the word "again" and asks, "What does it mean to you that it happened again?"

ts.socratic-summary.def: Stage 3 of Socratic dialogue: summarizing, often in writing and in the client's words, the information just gathered, to prepare for synthesis.
ts.socratic-summary.cw: The therapist pulls together what I just discovered so I can see it all at once.
ts.socratic-summary.ex: "Let me write down what you noticed: two people invited you out this month, and a colleague asked for your advice."

ts.socratic-synthesizing-question.def: Stage 4 of Socratic dialogue: a question asking the client to apply the summarized information to their original belief or concern.
ts.socratic-synthesizing-question.cw: A question that asks what all this new information means for my original worry.
ts.socratic-synthesizing-question.ex: "Looking at this list, how does it fit with the thought that nobody wants you around?"

ts.minimal-encourager.def: A brief sound, word or gesture that signals listening and invites the client to keep going, without adding content.
ts.minimal-encourager.cw: Small sounds or words, like "mm-hm", that show the therapist is with me.

ts.simple-reflection.def: A statement that gives back what the client said with little or no added meaning or emphasis.
ts.simple-reflection.cw: The therapist says back what I said, so I know they heard it.
ts.simple-reflection.ex: Client: "I'm tired all the time." Therapist: "You're exhausted."

ts.complex-reflection.def: A statement that reflects the client's words with added meaning or emphasis, such as an inferred feeling, meaning or the next unspoken step.
ts.complex-reflection.cw: The therapist puts into words what I meant, sometimes a bit more than I said.
ts.complex-reflection.ex: Client: "I'm tired all the time." Therapist: "And it's starting to feel like this will never lift."

ts.double-sided-reflection.def: A complex reflection capturing both sides of the client's ambivalence, usually joining them with "and" rather than "but".
ts.double-sided-reflection.cw: The therapist shows both sides of how I feel: the part that wants change and the part that doesn't.
ts.double-sided-reflection.ex: "Part of you wants to stop checking, and part of you worries something bad will happen if you do."

ts.amplified-reflection.def: A complex reflection that slightly overstates the client's sustain talk, without sarcasm, so the client can back away from the extreme position.
ts.amplified-reflection.cw: The therapist says my view a bit more strongly than I did, which makes me rethink it.
ts.amplified-reflection.ex: Client: "My drinking isn't a problem." Therapist: "There's nothing about it that concerns you at all."

ts.reflection-of-feeling.def: A reflection that names the client's emotion, stated or implied, often with its context, to show empathic understanding.
ts.reflection-of-feeling.cw: The therapist names the feeling I'm having, sometimes before I've found the word.
ts.reflection-of-feeling.ex: "You sound really hurt that she didn't call."

ts.reflection-of-meaning.def: A complex reflection naming the values, beliefs or personal significance beneath the client's account, beyond its facts and feelings.
ts.reflection-of-meaning.cw: The therapist helps me see why this matters so much to me.
ts.reflection-of-meaning.ex: "Being a reliable father sounds central to who you want to be."

ts.collecting-summary.def: A summary that gathers several related client statements, often change talk, and offers them back before inviting the client to continue.
ts.collecting-summary.cw: The therapist gathers up the things I've said so far and hands them back to me.
ts.collecting-summary.ex: "So far you've said you miss your friends, you're sleeping badly, and work feels pointless. What else?"

ts.linking-summary.def: A summary connecting what the client just said with something said earlier or in a past session, to show a pattern or ambivalence.
ts.linking-summary.cw: The therapist connects what I'm saying now with something I said before.
ts.linking-summary.ex: "That sounds like what happened with your sister last month: you stayed quiet, then felt resentful."

ts.transitional-summary.def: A summary that draws together a topic or session segment and signals a shift to a new task or topic.
ts.transitional-summary.cw: The therapist wraps up one topic before we move on to the next.
ts.transitional-summary.ex: "Let me sum up what we've covered about sleep before we turn to your action plan."

ts.capsule-summary.def: A brief CBT summary made at intervals in a session, condensing the main points or conclusion of an agenda item, ideally in the client's words.
ts.capsule-summary.cw: A quick recap partway through the session, so we're both clear on what we've worked out.
ts.capsule-summary.ex: "So the main thing we found is that the thought 'I'll fail' made you put off starting, and starting small helped."

ts.affirmation.def: A genuine statement recognizing the client's strengths, efforts, intentions or worth, focused on the client rather than on the therapist's approval.
ts.affirmation.cw: The therapist points out something I did well or a strength I have.
ts.affirmation.ex: "You came today even though getting out of the house was hard. That took real determination."

ts.empathic-statement.def: A compassionate or understanding comment conveying that the therapist grasps and cares how hard something is for the client.
ts.empathic-statement.cw: The therapist shows they get how hard this is for me.
ts.empathic-statement.ex: "That sounds really painful to go through."

ts.normalizing.def: Conveying, with accurate information, that an experience or symptom is common and understandable rather than a sign of being abnormal or broken.
ts.normalizing.cw: The therapist helps me see that what I'm going through is common, not a sign I'm broken.
ts.normalizing.ex: "Most people get unwanted, upsetting thoughts popping into their heads. Having them doesn't mean you want them."

ts.validation.def: Communicating that the client's emotions, thoughts or actions are understandable and make sense, given their history, situation or nature.
ts.validation.cw: The therapist lets me know my reactions make sense.
ts.validation.ex: "Given everything that happened, it makes sense you'd be wary of trusting people."

ts.validation-level-1.def: Listening and observing with full, nonjudgmental attention and interest, so the client sees they are taken seriously.
ts.validation-level-1.cw: The therapist pays full attention to me without judging.
ts.validation-level-1.ex: The therapist sets notes aside, keeps eye contact, and follows up on the detail the client just gave.

ts.validation-level-2.def: Accurately reflecting back the client's own stated feelings, thoughts and assumptions, without judgment, to communicate understanding.
ts.validation-level-2.cw: The therapist says back what I feel and think, so I know they understood.
ts.validation-level-2.ex: "You felt dismissed when your manager talked over you."

ts.validation-level-3.def: Putting into words feelings, thoughts or meanings the client has not stated, inferred from context or behavior, offered tentatively for correction.
ts.validation-level-3.cw: The therapist guesses what I'm feeling but haven't said, and checks if they're right.
ts.validation-level-3.ex: "I wonder if part of you also felt embarrassed. Is that close?"

ts.validation-level-4.def: Conveying that a response makes sense given the client's history, past learning or biology, even if it is not effective now.
ts.validation-level-4.cw: The therapist explains why I react this way, given what I've been through.
ts.validation-level-4.ex: "After years of being criticized at home, of course you brace yourself for criticism."

ts.validation-level-5.def: Conveying that the response is reasonable, normal or effective given the current situation, one most people would share.
ts.validation-level-5.cw: The therapist tells me most people would react the same way in my situation.
ts.validation-level-5.ex: "Anyone waiting for biopsy results would feel on edge."

ts.validation-level-6.def: Treating the client as a capable equal, not as fragile or merely a patient, and responding genuinely as one person to another.
ts.validation-level-6.cw: The therapist treats me as a capable equal and is real with me.
ts.validation-level-6.ex: The therapist responds to the client's good news with spontaneous, genuine delight rather than a scripted reflection.

ts.psychoeducation.def: Providing information about a condition, the CBT model or how a problem works, tailored to the client and checked for understanding.
ts.psychoeducation.cw: The therapist explains how my problem works in a way I can follow.
ts.psychoeducation.ex: "When you leave the supermarket, the anxiety drops fast, which teaches your brain that escaping is what kept you safe."

ts.giving-rationale.def: Explaining why a proposed task, technique or homework should help, linked to the client's formulation and goals, before asking them to try it.
ts.giving-rationale.cw: The therapist explains why we're doing something and how it connects to my goals.
ts.giving-rationale.ex: "An activity log shows us how what you do links to your mood, so we can pick changes that help."

ts.asking-permission.def: Asking the client's consent before offering information, advice, feedback or a sensitive topic, leaving the client free to decline.
ts.asking-permission.cw: The therapist asks if it's okay before sharing advice or raising something sensitive.
ts.asking-permission.ex: "Would it be all right if I shared what other people have found helpful?"

ts.elicit-provide-elicit.def: An information exchange sequence: ask what the client knows or wants to know, offer information briefly, then ask what they make of it.
ts.elicit-provide-elicit.cw: The therapist asks what I know, shares a bit, then asks what I think of it.
ts.elicit-provide-elicit.ex: "What do you already know about how sleep affects mood? ... Studies show ... What do you make of that?"

ts.advice-with-permission.def: Offering a suggestion or recommendation after the client asks or agrees, framed so the client remains free to decide.
ts.advice-with-permission.cw: The therapist offers a suggestion once I've said I want one, and I'm free to choose.
ts.advice-with-permission.ex: "Since you asked, one option is a fixed wake-up time. You know your life best, so see if it fits."

ts.emphasizing-autonomy.def: A statement highlighting the client's choice, control and right to decide about change, without blame.
ts.emphasizing-autonomy.cw: The therapist reminds me that the choices are mine to make.
ts.emphasizing-autonomy.ex: "It's your call whether to try this. You know what you're ready for."

ts.agenda-setting.def: Collaboratively deciding near the start of a session which topics or problems to cover, in what order, and for roughly how long.
ts.agenda-setting.cw: At the start, we agree together on what to talk about today.
ts.agenda-setting.ex: "What would you like on today's agenda? I'd also like to review the action plan. Which should we start with?"

ts.eliciting-feedback.def: Asking the client for reactions to the session, the therapist or a task, including what was unhelpful, and acting on the answer.
ts.eliciting-feedback.cw: The therapist asks what I thought of the session, including what didn't work for me.
ts.eliciting-feedback.ex: "Was there anything I said today that bothered you, or anything we should do differently next time?"

ts.checking-understanding.def: Confirming shared understanding: asking the client to restate a key point or plan, or asking whether the therapist's understanding is accurate.
ts.checking-understanding.cw: The therapist checks we understand each other, like asking me to put the plan in my own words.
ts.checking-understanding.ex: "Just so I know I explained it clearly, how would you describe the plan for this week?"

ts.collaborative-goal-setting.def: Working with the client to turn problems into specific, client-owned, measurable goals and agreeing on the tasks to reach them.
ts.collaborative-goal-setting.cw: We agree together on clear goals for therapy that matter to me.
ts.collaborative-goal-setting.ex: "If therapy went well, what would you be doing in three months that you aren't doing now?"

ts.reframing.def: Offering a different, plausible meaning for something the client described, which changes its emotional valence, for example from weakness to care.
ts.reframing.cw: The therapist offers a new way of looking at something that changes how it feels.
ts.reframing.ex: "You call it nagging. It also sounds like how much you care about his health."

ts.repair-acknowledge-rupture.def: Noticing and openly naming a strain in the relationship, such as withdrawal, appeasing or a complaint, instead of ignoring it.
ts.repair-acknowledge-rupture.cw: The therapist notices when something feels off between us and says so.
ts.repair-acknowledge-rupture.ex: "I notice you've gone quiet since I suggested the exposure task."

ts.repair-take-responsibility.def: Acknowledging, without defensiveness, the therapist's own part in a rupture, such as a misunderstanding or pushing too fast.
ts.repair-take-responsibility.cw: The therapist owns their part when something they did upset me.
ts.repair-take-responsibility.ex: "I think I pushed too quickly there, and that's on me."

ts.repair-metacommunication.def: Talking about what is happening between client and therapist in the moment, including disclosing the therapist's own experience of the interaction.
ts.repair-metacommunication.cw: The therapist talks openly about what's going on between us right now.
ts.repair-metacommunication.ex: "I'm feeling a bit stuck, as if we're both trying hard but missing each other. Does it feel that way to you?"

ts.repair-explore-rupture.def: Inviting the client to express negative thoughts and feelings about the therapist or therapy, and staying with them nondefensively.
ts.repair-explore-rupture.cw: The therapist invites me to say what I'm unhappy about in therapy, and really listens.
ts.repair-explore-rupture.ex: "What was it like when I suggested that? I'd really like to hear, even if it's critical."

ts.repair-change-task.def: Responding to a rupture by changing, pausing or adjusting the current task or goal so that it better fits the client.
ts.repair-change-task.cw: The therapist changes what we're doing when the current approach isn't working for me.
ts.repair-change-task.ex: "Let's set the thought record aside today and talk about what's been weighing on you."

ts.purposeful-silence.def: Deliberately pausing without speaking to give the client time to think, feel or continue, while remaining visibly attentive.
ts.purposeful-silence.cw: The therapist gives me quiet time to think or feel before saying more.
ts.purposeful-silence.ex: After the client says "I've never told anyone that," the therapist stays quietly attentive for several seconds.

ts.self-disclosure.def: Revealing something personal, such as a similar experience or feeling, briefly and for the client's benefit, then returning the focus to the client.
ts.self-disclosure.cw: The therapist briefly shares something about themselves that helps me, then turns back to me.
ts.self-disclosure.ex: "I've had to work on putting things off too. Starting with five minutes helped me. Could that fit for you?"

ts.humor.def: Light, well-timed humor attuned to the client and the alliance, used to ease tension or offer perspective, never at the client's expense.
ts.humor.cw: The therapist and I can share a light moment without it making fun of me.
ts.humor.ex: "So your anxiety has been working overtime as your unpaid personal assistant."

ts.righting-reflex.def: The urge to fix the client's problem by persuading, advising or arguing for change, which tends to provoke the client's counterarguments.
ts.righting-reflex.cw: The therapist jumps in to fix things or tell me what to do before understanding me.
ts.righting-reflex.ex: Avoid: "You really need to stop drinking. Have you tried just not buying it?"

ts.lecturing.def: Extended one-way explanation or information giving without checking the client's knowledge, interest or reaction.
ts.lecturing.cw: The therapist talks at me for a long time instead of with me.
ts.lecturing.ex: Avoid: several minutes on sleep hygiene rules with no question to the client.

ts.premature-reassurance.def: Reassuring before understanding the client's concern, or in reply to anxious reassurance seeking, which dismisses feelings and can maintain anxiety.
ts.premature-reassurance.cw: The therapist says everything will be fine before really hearing my worry.
ts.premature-reassurance.ex: Avoid: "Don't worry, I'm sure it's nothing serious."

ts.arguing.def: Directly disagreeing, correcting, criticizing or debating with the client in a way that sets the therapist against the client's view.
ts.arguing.cw: The therapist argues with me or tells me I'm wrong.
ts.arguing.ex: Avoid: "No, that's just not true, and you know it."

ts.interrupting.def: Cutting into the client's speech or changing topic before they finish, outside brief purposeful redirection, signaling that the therapist's agenda matters more.
ts.interrupting.cw: The therapist cuts me off before I've finished.
ts.interrupting.ex: Avoid: "Right, right, but let's get back to the homework" while the client is mid-sentence about a loss.

ts.labeling-client.def: Applying a fixed, judgmental label or diagnosis to the client as a person, such as "resistant" or "in denial", instead of describing behavior.
ts.labeling-client.cw: The therapist puts a label on me instead of seeing me as a person.
ts.labeling-client.ex: Avoid: "The problem is that you're in denial."

ts.premature-advice.def: Telling the client what to do before understanding the problem or getting permission, often solving the wrong problem.
ts.premature-advice.cw: The therapist tells me what to do before understanding my situation or asking if I want advice.
ts.premature-advice.ex: Avoid: "You should just talk to your boss about it," a minute after hearing the problem.

ts.tentative-hypothesis.def: Offering an inference about a thought, belief or pattern as a possibility the client can confirm or correct, never stated as fact.
ts.tentative-hypothesis.cw: The therapist shares a guess about what might be going on and asks if it fits.
ts.tentative-hypothesis.ex: "I might be off here, so tell me if this doesn't fit. I wonder if 'useless' is the word that keeps coming back."

ts.instilling-hope.def: Building realistic expectation of benefit through a credible, personalized rationale, honest answers about likely progress, and visible evidence of change, without promising outcomes.
ts.instilling-hope.cw: The therapist helps me see realistic reasons to expect things can improve, without empty promises.
ts.instilling-hope.ex: "I can't promise, but this approach helps many people with this problem, and we'll check every few weeks whether it's helping you."

ts.highlighting-progress.def: Drawing the client's attention to specific, measured improvement and crediting their own actions for it, so early gains build hope and engagement.
ts.highlighting-progress.cw: The therapist points out what has improved, with numbers, and what I did to make it happen.
ts.highlighting-progress.ex: "Two weeks ago you rated the dread at 80. Today it's 55. What did you do differently?"

ts.nonverbal-attunement.def: Using posture, facial expression, eye contact, pace and tone of voice that fit the client's state and match the therapist's words.
ts.nonverbal-attunement.cw: The therapist's face, voice and pace show they are with me and match what they say.
ts.nonverbal-attunement.ex: With a tearful client, the therapist slows down, softens their voice and keeps a calm, open posture.

ts.using-client-words.def: Repeating the client's own key words, images and metaphors in reflections and summaries instead of translating them into technical terms.
ts.using-client-words.cw: The therapist uses my words and images, not jargon.
ts.using-client-words.ex: "You called it 'the fog'. When the fog comes down, what happens next?"

ts.plain-language.def: Explaining ideas in everyday words and short sentences, adding a technical term only after the plain version and only if it helps.
ts.plain-language.cw: The therapist explains things in everyday words I can follow.
ts.plain-language.ex: "Thoughts that pop into your head" before "automatic thoughts".

ts.redirecting-to-agenda.def: Politely interrupting a peripheral or circular discussion with a brief summary and a link back to the agreed agenda item.
ts.redirecting-to-agenda.cw: The therapist kindly steers us back to what I said matters most today.
ts.redirecting-to-agenda.ex: "Can I stop you there for a moment? I want to make sure we get to the panic at work, which you said mattered most today."

ts.grounding.def: Bringing a dissociating or overwhelmed client back to the present by orienting to time and place and directing attention to concrete sensations.
ts.grounding.cw: The therapist helps me come back to the here and now by noticing what I can sense.
ts.grounding.ex: "Can you feel your feet on the floor? Tell me three things you can see in this room."

ts.de-escalation.def: Responding to anger or agitation with calm, concise speech, respectful distance, honest agreement where possible, clear limits and choices.
ts.de-escalation.cw: When I'm very angry, the therapist stays calm, listens and helps me settle.
ts.de-escalation.ex: "You're really angry, and you have good reason to be upset about the wait. I want to understand. Can we sit down and go through it?"

ts.direct-suicide-question.def: Asking plainly and calmly whether the client is thinking about suicide when hopelessness or distress appears, then assessing risk if indicated.
ts.direct-suicide-question.cw: The therapist asks me straight out about thoughts of suicide, so we can keep me safe.
ts.direct-suicide-question.ex: "Sometimes when people feel this hopeless they think about ending their life. Has that been on your mind?"

tt.loss-and-defeat.def: Thoughts that something valued has been lost or that one has been beaten or diminished: a person, role, status, health or goal.
tt.loss-and-defeat.cw: Thoughts about losing something or someone important, or feeling beaten down.
tt.loss-and-defeat.ex: "Since the divorce, I've lost everything that mattered."

tt.inadequacy-and-failure.def: Thoughts that one is incompetent, weak or not good enough to meet demands, and has failed or will fail.
tt.inadequacy-and-failure.cw: Thoughts that you're not capable or good enough, or that you keep failing.
tt.inadequacy-and-failure.ex: "I can't do anything right at work."

tt.abandonment-and-rejection.def: Thoughts that one is unlovable or will be rejected, left or let down by the people one depends on.
tt.abandonment-and-rejection.cw: Thoughts that people you care about will leave you or don't really want you.
tt.abandonment-and-rejection.ex: "He'll get bored of me and leave, like everyone else."

tt.hopelessness.def: Thoughts that the future is bleak, problems will not improve and nothing one does will make a difference. A key suicide risk signal.
tt.hopelessness.cw: Thoughts that things will never get better, no matter what you do.
tt.hopelessness.ex: "There's no point. It's always going to be like this."

tt.burdensomeness.def: Thoughts that one is a liability to others and that they would be better off without one, often fused with self-hatred. Raises suicide risk.
tt.burdensomeness.cw: Thoughts that you're a burden and others would be better off without you.
tt.burdensomeness.ex: "My family would be better off if I wasn't here."

tt.entrapment.def: Thoughts that one is trapped in an intolerable situation or inner pain with no way out, often following defeat or humiliation.
tt.entrapment.cw: Feeling stuck in unbearable pain or circumstances with no way out.
tt.entrapment.ex: "I can't escape this, and I can't keep living like this."

tt.threat-and-danger.def: Thoughts that physical or psychological harm is likely or imminent in a situation; the core content of anxiety and fear.
tt.threat-and-danger.cw: Thoughts that something dangerous or harmful is about to happen.
tt.threat-and-danger.ex: "Something bad will happen if I leave the house."

tt.vulnerability.def: Thoughts that one is weak, exposed or unable to protect oneself or cope with threat, and that help is unavailable.
tt.vulnerability.cw: Thoughts that you couldn't protect yourself or cope if something went wrong.
tt.vulnerability.ex: "If something happens, I'll be on my own and helpless."

tt.physical-catastrophe.def: Thoughts that bodily sensations signal an immediate disaster such as a heart attack, suffocation, fainting or collapse.
tt.physical-catastrophe.cw: Thoughts that a racing heart or dizziness means something terrible is happening right now.
tt.physical-catastrophe.ex: "My heart is pounding. I'm having a heart attack."

tt.serious-illness.def: Thoughts that benign symptoms or medical uncertainty mean one has, or will develop, a serious disease that has been missed.
tt.serious-illness.cw: Thoughts that a symptom means you have a serious illness doctors have missed.
tt.serious-illness.ex: "This headache means I have a brain tumor."

tt.loss-of-control.def: Thoughts that one will lose control of mind, body, emotions or behavior, for example going mad, acting on an impulse or being overwhelmed.
tt.loss-of-control.cw: Thoughts that you'll lose control, go crazy, or do something you can't stop.
tt.loss-of-control.ex: "If this feeling gets any stronger, I'll lose my mind."

tt.negative-evaluation.def: Thoughts that others are noticing and judging one negatively, that one will appear anxious, awkward or inadequate and lose status or acceptance.
tt.negative-evaluation.cw: Thoughts that people are judging you and will think badly of you.
tt.negative-evaluation.ex: "They can see I'm blushing. They'll think I'm weird."

tt.sleep-loss-consequences.def: Thoughts that one will not sleep and that poor sleep will seriously harm health, mood or next-day functioning.
tt.sleep-loss-consequences.cw: Thoughts that you won't sleep and that tomorrow, or your health, will be ruined.
tt.sleep-loss-consequences.ex: "If I don't fall asleep now, I'll fall apart at work tomorrow."

tt.contamination.def: Thoughts that one is or will become dirty, infected or polluted through contact with substances, places or people, and may spread harm.
tt.contamination.cw: Thoughts that you're dirty or infected, or could spread germs or harm.
tt.contamination.ex: "I touched the door handle. Now I'll make my kids sick."

tt.inflated-responsibility.def: Thoughts whose content is being to blame for possible harm: that one could cause it, must prevent it, and failing to act equals causing it.
tt.inflated-responsibility.cw: Thoughts that it's up to you to stop anything bad happening, and it's your fault if it does.
tt.inflated-responsibility.ex: "If I don't check the stove again and there's a fire, it'll be my fault."

tt.significance-of-thoughts.def: Thoughts whose content is that one's intrusive or uncontrolled thoughts are meaningful, dangerous or revealing of one's character, and must be controlled.
tt.significance-of-thoughts.cw: Thoughts that having an upsetting thought means something bad about you or is dangerous.
tt.significance-of-thoughts.ex: "Having this thought about hurting my baby means I'm a monster."

tt.violation-and-unfairness.def: Thoughts that one has been wronged, treated unfairly, disrespected or had important rules broken by others, often seen as intentional.
tt.violation-and-unfairness.cw: Thoughts that someone treated you unfairly or broke the rules on purpose.
tt.violation-and-unfairness.ex: "She deliberately humiliated me in front of everyone."

tt.transgression.def: Thoughts that one has done something wrong, broken one's own moral code or hurt someone, focused on the act rather than the whole self.
tt.transgression.cw: Thoughts that you did something wrong or hurt someone and should have acted differently.
tt.transgression.ex: "I snapped at my daughter. That was a terrible thing to do."

tt.defect-and-exposure.def: Thoughts that the self is fundamentally flawed, bad or unacceptable, and that others will discover it and reject or humiliate one.
tt.defect-and-exposure.cw: Thoughts that something is deeply wrong with you and people will find out.
tt.defect-and-exposure.ex: "If they knew the real me, they'd be disgusted."

tt.permanent-change-after-trauma.def: Thoughts after trauma that one has been permanently damaged or changed, and that one's life, body or future is ruined beyond recovery.
tt.permanent-change-after-trauma.cw: Thoughts that what happened has changed or damaged you for good.
tt.permanent-change-after-trauma.ex: "I'll never be the person I was. He ruined my life."

tt.shape-weight-and-eating-control.def: Thoughts that one looks fat, has gained weight, has eaten too much or lost control over eating, and must restrict or compensate.
tt.shape-weight-and-eating-control.cw: Thoughts that you look fat, ate too much or lost control, and need to make up for it.
tt.shape-weight-and-eating-control.ex: "I've eaten far too much. I look huge. I have to skip dinner."

tt.appearance-defect.def: Thoughts that a specific feature of one's appearance is defective or ugly, is noticed by others and is central to one's worth.
tt.appearance-defect.cw: Thoughts that part of how you look is ugly or wrong and others notice it.
tt.appearance-defect.ex: "Everyone is staring at my nose. It's hideous."

tt.persecution.def: Thoughts that others intend to cause one harm, physical, psychological or social, now or in the future.
tt.persecution.cw: Thoughts that other people are deliberately out to harm you.
tt.persecution.ex: "My neighbors are plotting to get rid of me."

tt.personal-gain-and-grandiosity.def: Inflated thoughts about one's abilities, importance and prospects, overestimating gains and underestimating risks; typical of hypomania and mania.
tt.personal-gain-and-grandiosity.cw: Thoughts that you're unstoppable, special or certain to succeed, so risks don't matter.
tt.personal-gain-and-grandiosity.ex: "I've had a brilliant idea. I'll make a fortune and nothing can go wrong."

bf.d: Longitudinal factors in a five Ps formulation, grouped predisposing (early experiences, temperament, family history, developmental and health conditions), precipitating (life events before onset or worsening) and protective (supports, skills, strengths). Used by the predisposing, precipitating and protective slots of the five Ps formulation and the relevant childhood data box of the cognitive conceptualization diagram. Perpetuating factors are coded in mp and bh; in-the-moment triggers in sit.

bh.d: Observable and covert behaviors at the situation level: what the client does, or stops doing, in response to a trigger. Fills the behavior slots of five-part, cognitive model and disorder-specific maintenance formulations. Enduring cross-situational patterns are in cs; processes such as rumination, worry, thought suppression and self-focused attention are in mp; risk levels are in rk.

bs.d: Physical sensations a client notices, used in the physical reactions slot of the five-part model and in panic, health anxiety, insomnia, eating and anger formulations; rated for intensity (0 to 100). Code the sensation here; a catastrophic reading of it is a thought, and what the client does about it is a behavior.

cd.d: Systematic errors in how automatic thoughts process information (how a thought is biased, not what it is about). Tags automatic thoughts and hot thoughts in five-part, cognitive model and thought record formulation slots. Overlaps resolved: tunnel vision is an alias of mental filter, probability overestimation of fortune telling, awfulizing of catastrophizing.

cs.d: Enduring coping patterns a client uses across situations. Group compensatory holds strategies developed to cope with core beliefs and conditional assumptions, as in the coping strategies box of the cognitive conceptualization diagram. Group adaptive holds flexible, helpful coping that a formulation names as strengths or treatment goals. Situation-level acts are in bh.

cb.d: Global, rigid beliefs about the self (helpless, unlovable and worthless clusters, plus adaptive counterparts), others, the world and the future. Fills the core belief slot of the cognitive conceptualization diagram and longitudinal formulations. Each concept carries about: self, others, world or future.

em.d: Emotions a client names and rates for intensity (0 to 100) in thought records and in the emotions slot of formulation models, grouped into families, with valence (positive or negative hedonic tone). Code single feeling words here; words such as worthless, useless or a failure are thoughts or beliefs and belong in thought or belief schemes, not here. Positive emotions support activity monitoring and protective factors.

ib.d: Rules, conditional assumptions and attitudes that link core beliefs to automatic thoughts and coping, including metacognitive, OCD, emotion, health, sleep, eating, substance and mood-specific beliefs. Fills the intermediate beliefs slot of the cognitive conceptualization diagram. Each concept carries kind: rule, assumption or attitude. It also holds the belief domains of the OCD and eating disorder models: inflated responsibility, thought-action fusion and overvaluation of shape and weight.

iv.d: Catalog of CBT interventions and techniques a therapist delivers, grouped cognitive, behavioral, exposure, emotion and compassion, relational and session process, and condition-specific. Used to code the intervention or treatment-target slots of a formulation and treatment plan. Client coping actions belong in cs; therapist competencies in ts; instruments in ms.

mp.d: Transdiagnostic and disorder-specific processes that keep a problem going once it has started: avoidance and safety seeking, repetitive negative thinking, attention, memory and reasoning biases, appraisals of intrusions, bodies and trauma, and eating, sleep, mood, interpersonal, substance use and bipolar cycles. Fills the maintenance (what keeps it going) slots and feedback links of formulation models. Specific behaviors, beliefs and thinking traps live in the bh, cs, cb, ib and cd schemes; concepts here name the cycle or process that links them. Belief content that a process acts on (inflated responsibility, thought-action fusion, overvaluation of shape and weight) is coded in ib.

ms.d: Standardized and idiographic instruments used in CBT for screening, severity, outcome, process, competence and risk monitoring. Each concept carries page, construct, items (core or main-form item count), format, licensing (public-domain: reproduce without a request; free-with-permission: copyrighted but free for clinical or non-commercial use under stated terms or on request; proprietary: purchase or paid license), licensing_note and population. Used to tag measurement slots and pages.

rk.d: Risk documentation codes in six groups: static risk factors (historical, unchangeable), dynamic risk factors (current, changeable), warning signs (near-term changes over hours to days), protective factors, harm-to-others indicators and safeguarding indicators. Used by the 02-risk pages, risk sections of intake records and session notes, and risk notes alongside a formulation. The codes organize clinical judgment; they are not a prediction score, since risk factors predict suicide only slightly better than chance and NICE advises against risk stratification for prediction. Deliberately contains no method or lethality detail. Emotions, beliefs, behaviors and life events in general live in the em, tt, cb, bh, sit and bf schemes, and rk concepts link to them with related: code hopelessness, perceived burdensomeness and entrapment with tt; social isolation, social support, coping skills, community belonging, chronic illness or pain and a rise in substance use with bf; social withdrawal and reckless behavior with bh.

sit.d: Categories of external situations and internal events that set off automatic thoughts, emotions, body sensations, urges or behavior in the here and now. Used by the Situation or Trigger slot of the five-part model, the cognitive conceptualization diagram and maintenance cycles, and for listing current triggers. Code the reaction itself in em, bs, tt or bh; code life events and history in bf.

ts.d: A coding vocabulary for therapist responses in session, so a transcript turn, a supervision note or a tool response can be labeled. Codes map to MITI 4 and MISC 2.5 behavior codes where those exist (field codes). Not used by formulation slots; used by responding-in-session, alliance and session-structure pages. Group avoid holds unhelpful responses.

tt.d: What automatic thoughts are about: the content themes that, under Beck's content-specificity hypothesis, characterize particular emotions and disorders. Tags the theme of automatic thoughts and hot thoughts in formulation slots. Each concept carries emotions (em ids of the emotions the theme typically drives) and conditions (topic values from _schema.md section 5). A theme is the content of in-the-moment thoughts; the matching enduring beliefs are in cb and ib. The suicide-relevant themes (hopelessness, burdensomeness, entrapment) are coded here, and rk links to them.

fm.five-part.s: Maps one recent episode as a situation plus four interacting parts: thoughts, emotions, physical reactions and behaviors.
fm.five-part.when: Early sessions with any presenting problem, to socialize the client to CBT and map a specific recent episode together.

slots.q: When was the last time this happened? Where were you, who was there, what was going on?
What was going through your mind just then? What images or memories came up?
What did you feel? Can you name it in one word?
What did you notice in your body?
What did you do, or stop yourself from doing?

fm.cognitive-conceptualization-diagram.s: Links life history to core beliefs, conditional assumptions and coping strategies, then shows how they play out in three typical situations.
fm.cognitive-conceptualization-diagram.when: Once several situations have been mapped and the client is ready to understand why the same patterns recur.

slots.q: What experiences growing up, or before this episode began, shaped how you see yourself, others and the world?
If that thought were true, what would it say about you? About other people?
What rules do you live by to cope with that belief? If you did or did not do that, what would happen?
What do you do to protect yourself so that belief does not come true or show?
What was the situation? Where were you and what was happening?
What was going through your mind?
If that thought were true, what would it mean to you?
What did you feel?
What did you do then?
What was the situation? Where were you and what was happening?
What was going through your mind?
If that thought were true, what would it mean to you?
What did you feel?
What did you do then?
What was the situation? Where were you and what was happening?
What was going through your mind?
If that thought were true, what would it mean to you?
What did you feel?
What did you do then?

fm.five-ps.s: Organizes the presenting problem with predisposing, precipitating, perpetuating and protective factors.
fm.five-ps.when: At the end of assessment, to summarize history and current maintenance in one page and point to treatment targets and strengths.

slots.q: What was happening in your life when this started or got worse?
What in your history might have made you more vulnerable to this?
What are the main difficulties you want help with, in your own words?
What keeps this going now, even when you try to change it?
What helps, even a little? What strengths and support do you have?

fm.functional-analysis-abc.s: Links one specific target behavior to its antecedents and to its short- and long-term consequences, to find the function that keeps it going.
fm.functional-analysis-abc.when: A specific problem behavior (avoidance, bingeing, drinking, self-injury, outbursts, checking) whose triggers and reinforcers must be found before choosing interventions.

slots.q: Where were you, who was there, and what had just happened?
What did the behavior do for you right away?
What happened in the first minutes after?
What were you feeling, thinking or sensing just before?
What exactly did you do, how often and for how long?
What did it cost you later that day, that week or longer?
What could meet the same need at less cost, and what will we change first?

fm.behavior-chain.s: Traces one episode of a problem behavior link by link, from vulnerability factors and the prompting event to consequences, with a planned solution under each link.
fm.behavior-chain.when: Self-harm, suicidal behavior, bingeing, substance use or another emotion-driven behavior that recurs, to find where a skillful response could break the chain.

slots.q: What made you more vulnerable that day: sleep, illness, hunger, substances, stress?
What happened right before the chain started?
Moment by moment, what did you think, feel, sense and do next?
What exactly did you do?
What happened right after, and later, for you and for others?
What could lower your vulnerability next time?

slots.l: Prevent or handle the prompting event
slots.q: How could you avoid that event, or meet it differently?
At which link could you have used a skill, and which one?
What can you do to repair the harm the behavior caused?

fm.vicious-flower.s: Shows depression at the center with six petals, each a loop that feeds and is fed by the depression.
